aggro.name: Aggro
aggro.html: Aggro fought as a warrior for Ascension across 57 raids between 6 October 2019 and 13 May 2020, one of the guild's earliest sustained warriors. Seven outside reports overlap the run, from 13 November 2019 to 15 March 2020, with none before or after. No landmark or loot award is documented for Aggro.

akikiie.name: Akikiie
akikiie.html:
Aki, Silveh on Discord, built the house the Dusk era lived in: the first message in the entire officer-chat archive is him setting up the Ninjas server in April 2020, gated roles and class channels and all. He was a Ninjas officer, a warrior with fifty-eight raids, and a steady tactical voice through the AQ progression, explaining Huhuran nature-resistance splits in paragraphs while others argued in fragments.

His guild life ended on a single pull. On 17 September 2020 he pulled at the Ahn'Qiraj entrance with nobody ready. The world buffs died, Ulfhild rage-quit, and three days of officer warfare followed. Aki owned it completely: "I'll happily apologise and take the blame for it. It's not my intent to hide from it." Then he asked the question underneath the whole affair, whether he actually enjoyed a game where a single wipe could ruin forty people's evening. He decided he didn't, and left within the week. The archive remembers him as the architect of the guild's home and the first casualty of its seriousness.

alcliff.name: Alcliff
alcliff.html:
Alcliff was a paladin with three Sleep raids, ten Dusk raids and one personal PUG. He stayed through Dusk's first guild-only Naxxramas night, and seventeen awards trace his gearing from Lawbringer pieces into the autumn.

Twenty-two outside reports overlap his local tenure and seven follow it. Officer chat on 13 December records that Alcliff and Docthor were both in Exsul, confirming the destination independently of the report cluster.

aldrei.name: Aldrei
aldrei.html: Aldrei was a priest with eighteen Ninjas raids and one Dusk appearance between February and August 2020. Ten outside reports overlap that tenure. No activity has been found before the local opening or after the final raid.

amandil.name: Amandil
amandil.html:
Amandil raided as a warlock through Sleep's founding stretch, 41 raids between 13 November 2019 and 22 March 2020. He was there for the very first surviving 10/10 Molten Core clear on the opening night, the first surviving Onyxia kill four days later, and the first Nefarian kill the following February, three of the earliest "first" landmarks the archive records.

He also shows up in the guild's day-to-day logistics: in February 2020 Rocka substituted for him at an officer meeting when he couldn't make it, and in March he took part in an open Discord conversation with Docthor and Shakey about how the guild was running. No outside reports exist before, during, or after his tenure, so the record has nothing to say about where he went once his raids stopped.

amarah.name: Amarah
amarah.html: Amarah was a druid with 122 logged raids from 13 February 2020 through 11 April 2021. The lineage runs through 58 Ninjas raids, 31 Dusk raids, 26 Ascension raids, five joint sessions, and two personal pugs. Amarah was present for the first C'Thun and Ouro kills, the first complete 9/9 Ahn'Qiraj clear, both openings of Naxxramas, and the first Kel'Thuzad kill. Amarah and Juud were the only two players from the former Ninjas roster in that first-kill lineup. Nine recorded awards include Eye of C'Thun, Guise of the Devourer, and two early pieces of Naxxramas tier armor.

amberlynreid.name: Amberlynreid
amberlynreid.html: Amberlynreid raided as a rogue for Ascension 66 times between 15 March 2020 and 11 April 2021, one of those a personal PUG appearance rather than a guild raid. Sixteen outside reports overlap the run, from 8 April to 11 November 2020, with none before or after. No landmark or loot award is documented.

amorise.name: Amorise
amorise.html: Amorise was a rogue with ten Ascension guild raids and one personal PUG between February and July 2020. Five outside reports predate the guild tenure and one overlaps it. No later appearance has been found.

anerd.name: Anerd
anerd.html: Anerd was a warrior in Ascension's opening roster with ten guild raids from October through November 2019. Two outside reports overlap that tenure. No activity has been found before it or after it.

annafrank.name: Annafrank
annafrank.html: Annafrank raided as a rogue for Sleep 50 times between 4 December 2019 and 6 May 2020, present for the first Nefarian kill, and picked up two loot awards that spring: Bloodfang Gloves and Cloak of Firemaw. In February 2020, the guild's own raider-overview documents named Annafrank as one of five rogues holding a confirmed raider spot, alongside Jellopy, Kodf, Pricelez and Rainer. No outside reports exist before, during, or after the run, so nothing places this character elsewhere once the raids stop.

anthroy.name: Anthroy
anthroy.html: Anthroy raided as a warrior for Ascension thirty-five times between January and August 2020. Seven outside reports predate his local debut and ten overlap the tenure. The completed character search contains no appearance after his final Ascension raid.

antzi.name: Antzi
antzi.html:
Antzi ran the rogues — before the merger in Ninjas, after it in Dusk — and brought to the officer chat a philosophy he repeated until everyone could recite it: focus is respect. He didn't care if you came unbuffed; he cared if you wasted thirty-nine other people's evening. "I play this game for the community," he wrote in one of the autumn's better manifestos, and meant it literally — his rogues never once made loot drama, a record he defended with visible pride.

His temper was the cost of the conviction. The September crises pulled him into shouting matches with Divinestorm ("no brain pull"), with Rockafella ("stick to ur lock"), and into the Band of Accuria blowup where he heard himself called stupid and demanded it never happen again. But the record consistently shows the anger pointing somewhere real: at carelessness, at gift-loot logic, at anything that treated the raid's time as free. When he admitted he'd talked his rogues out of quitting "with arguments I don't even believe," it was the most honest sentence of the whole autumn.

His final logged Dusk raid was 24 September. Sixty later reports cover forty dates through 16 May 2021, with Pawsz present on thirty-four and Banamahs on twenty-nine. The changing uploaders and repeated PUG titles show that they continued raiding together in a stable PUG circuit after Dusk. None matches Decimation's thirty-eight-report historical guild feed, so the logs do not identify a later guild Antzi joined.

appelflap.name: Appelflap
appelflap.html: Appelflap raided as a warlock for Ascension across 47 raids between 27 February and 7 December 2020, one of them a personal PUG. Twenty-four outside reports predate the run, a larger pre-history than most in this batch, and 11 more overlap it, ending 18 November 2020, with none afterward. No landmark or loot award is documented.

arcanefarts.name: Arcanefarts
arcanefarts.html:
Arcanefarts was a mage who joined the Ninjas roster in June and crossed into Dusk. He completed thirty-four guild raids, including the first C'Thun and Ouro kills, plus one personal PUG in the local archive. Officer chat later placed him among the players balancing Dusk raids with other raid plans.

His post-tenure history is substantial: fifty-two reports from November 2020 through May 2021. The current metadata proves continued raiding but does not establish a destination guild.

arlin.name: Arlin
arlin.html: Arlin was a priest in Ascension with twenty-six guild raids from February through May 2020. Thirteen reports predate that tenure and twelve overlap it. A single appearance two weeks after the final Ascension raid is the only later trace.

artimis.name: Artimis
artimis.html:
Artimis joined Dejvid's young guild in the autumn of 2019 and was soon running it in practice — formally from February 2020, when Dejvid handed over the reins. He ran it the way he ran everything: with spreadsheets. The attendance workbook was his. So was the loot log, started 2020-03-29 with a plea that class leaders post every drop, and the raider-rank system with its promise that showing up mattered. Most of it outlived his tenure. As a hunter he negotiated the early Rhok'delar queue one player at a time, then finished his own bow around 11 November 2019. As an alchemist he ran a one-man consumables service, mailing flasks to tanks and crafting anything anyone needed. His priest alt Lege healed whenever the roster came up short.

He gave the guild away twice. In early 2020 he offered the leadership to Kodf, who declined; in August 2020, minutes after a Nefarian kill, he told the raid that Divinestorm would be the new Guild Master and thanked everyone for their trust — handing over the guild mid-raid, in the same breath as a boss kill. He stayed on as the institutional memory: teaching the spreadsheets, mediating disputes, and writing the rules other people argued about.

The governing instinct underneath the spreadsheets was collective. In April, while the mage class argued over its leader, he refused to act as a "solo ruler" and put the decision to the officers. That habit made him slower than a dictator and harder to blame alone, which was usually the point.

December 2020 made him the story's protagonist against his will. When the Ascension merge cut the roster to twenty and the promises of the raider-rank system stopped being honoured, Artimis wrote a five-point proposal (raiders before members, whole-lockout spots, collective bench decisions) and asked members to strike. He himself had been benched from every single Four Horsemen attempt. The strike never happened; the guild dissolved into Ascension two days later. He kept raiding into 2021, kept the records, and years later those records became this site.

The bench had already pushed him into a second raid life. From November he guest-healed external gold-bid raids on Lege because the priest had hit the guild's alt-loot ceiling. That ended in the final days of December, when his child arrived and weekend raid invitations stopped fitting the life around them.

askcandy.name: Askcandy
askcandy.html:
Askcandy was a hunter whose route crossed Sleep, Ninjas and Dusk. Twenty-four guild raids and two personal PUGs survive from July 2020 into January 2021. He joined the first C'Thun and Ouro kills and Dusk's first full Ahn'Qiraj clear; Dragonstalker's Legguards are his documented loot award.

Nineteen outside reports overlap the tenure. Fifteen more continue through April 2021, showing later activity without a confirmed destination.

aurun.name: Aurun
aurun.html: Aurun was a warrior in Ascension with twelve guild raids from November through December 2019. One outside report overlaps the first local date. No activity has been found before the tenure or after it.

baguette.name: Baguette
baguette.html: Baguette was a mage in Ascension's earliest roster with sixteen guild raids from October through December 2019. Two outside reports overlap that period. Fifty-eight later reports continue through July 2020, revealing a much larger second raid history whose guild is not identified.

balabadoba.name: Balabadoba
balabadoba.html: Balabadoba was a warlock on Sleep's first surviving roster. His eighteen guild raids include the first complete Molten Core report and the first logged Onyxia kill in November 2019. One external report overlaps the tenure; none appears before it or after it.

banamahs.name: Banamahs
banamahs.html:
Banamahs led the Thursday mages and thought about guilds the way an economist thinks about fisheries: the resource is your members' time and goodwill, and every scuffed raid overfishes it. "Longevity is the key to this game," he wrote in September, "but if you burn resources too quickly, people quit." He said it about continuation raids, about split-run chaos, about consumable costs — and the autumn kept proving him right.

He was the calm half of the Ninjas bloc: building loot-overview spreadsheets other class leaders copied, absorbing a mage exodus (three top-geared mages gone in a week) with recruitment plans instead of drama, and cutting through the era's worst arguments with lines like "this wasn't a case of afk players — we were not ready to pull." His tribute to Ulfhild doubles as his own epitaph for the era: if everyone pumped that hard, the raid would take forty-five minutes.

On 3 October he announced that he was leaving, but kept his alt Banama in Dusk "to be able to catch up." Nine minutes later Luivi called him "another Decimation recruit." The economist had followed his own warning: once the group's goodwill was spent, he moved on.

The later logs add a second, separate thread: seventy-one reports across forty-four dates, with Pawsz present on thirty-five and Antzi on twenty-nine. Those reports belong to a stable PUG circuit under several uploaders. None matches Decimation's thirty-eight-report historical guild feed. The contemporary recruitment message, not these later raids, remains the evidence for Banamahs's guild destination.

bananabread.name: Bananabread
bananabread.html:
Bananabread was a priest who completed nineteen Ninjas raids and nine Dusk raids, plus one personal PUG. He joined the first C'Thun and Ouro kills, and the loot record preserves Sand Reaver Wristguards from an Ahn'Qiraj 20 run.

Twenty reports predate his June arrival and twelve overlap the local tenure. Thirty-three later reports continue from October 2020 through May 2021, showing a substantial second raid history without a confirmed guild name.

barin.name: Barin
barin.html:
Barin joined the closing act as a warrior. His thirty-seven guild raids include Dusk's first joint Naxxramas night with Ascension and the first Kel'Thuzad kill eleven days later. Most of his local record belongs to Ascension, with five joint raids preserving the bridge between the two guilds.

The wider history is much longer than the local one: 104 reports predate his October arrival and twenty-seven overlap it. Five reports after the final Ascension appearance continue into May 2021, but they do not establish a named destination.

bazookabill.name: Bazookabill
bazookabill.html: Bazookabill was a hunter in Ninjas with twenty-two guild raids from March through June 2020. Ten outside reports overlap that tenure. No report has been found before the local opening or after his final raid.

bbfly.name: Bbfly
bbfly.html: Bbfly was a priest on Sleep's original surviving roster. Twenty-five guild raids begin with the first complete Molten Core report in November 2019, and one personal PUG closes the local record in June 2020. Two outside reports overlap that final month; no broader later history has been found.

bearinpants.name: Bearinpants
bearinpants.html:
Bearinpants was a warrior who arrived late in Ascension's Naxxramas season. Twenty guild raids and one personal PUG survive from January through April 2021. His earlier history is far larger: 111 reports precede the local tenure.

Eight outside reports overlap Ascension and six more continue into May. Those later reports preserve shared activity with former roster members, not a confirmed destination guild.

bein.name: Bein
bein.html: Bein was a mage who completed fourteen Ninjas raids and one Dusk raid in the summer of 2020. Eleven outside reports predate the local tenure and three overlap it. No later appearance has been found.

bigmag.name: Bigmag
bigmag.html: Bigmag was a mage whose twenty-one guild raids touched Sleep once, Ninjas six times and Dusk fourteen times. He joined the first C'Thun and Ouro kills and Dusk's first complete Ahn'Qiraj clear. Four external reports overlap the tenure; none follows it.

biterx.name: Biterx
biterx.html: Biterx was a warrior from the Ascension side of the wider archive, with 106 logged raids between 4 December 2019 and 7 April 2021. The inventory assigns 102 to Ascension, two to joint Dusk–Ascension raids, and two to personal pugs. Two outside reports precede this span and 21 external reports fall within it; they show activity only, while no named landmark or loot award is currently documented for Biterx.

bluerothmans.name: Bluerothmans
bluerothmans.html: Bluerothmans was a paladin in Ascension with nineteen guild raids from April through June 2020. Fifty-two reports predate that short local tenure, and forty-one more continue from July 2020 through May 2021. The evidence shows a long independent raid history but does not currently name a later guild.

bobag.name: Bobag
bobag.html:
Bobag was a paladin whose guild record stretches from Sleep's first winter into Ascension's Naxxramas season. Twenty-four Sleep raids, seven Dusk raids and two Ascension raids survive. He was there for the first Nefarian kill, and his five recorded awards include Aurastone Hammer and Judgement Spaulders.

The completed wider search finds no reports outside the local archive, making Bobag's cross-guild path visible entirely through the project's own records.

borel.name: Borel
borel.html: Borel was a priest from the Ascension side of the wider archive, with 116 logged raids between 20 November 2019 and 14 April 2021. The inventory assigns 114 sessions to Ascension and two to the joint Dusk–Ascension roster. Borel was in the lineup for the first Kel'Thuzad kill on 20 December 2020. A broader report search found nine reports before the logged span, 31 external reports during it, and ten afterward; these show continued Warcraft activity without proving guild membership.

bosstus.name: Bosstus
bosstus.html: Bosstus was a hunter with fourteen Dusk raids and two personal PUGs during the Ahn'Qiraj autumn. Five awards include Dragonstalker's Gauntlets and Scaled Sand Reaver Leggings. Two external reports overlap the tenure, and none appears afterward.

boxya.name: Boxya
boxya.html: Boxya's guild career is a two-act comedy of timing. Recruited by Luivi as a friend of Wandolina, he signed up for a September raid, never showed, and left the guild the next day. Yet by December he was back and suddenly indispensable: picked as one of Dusk's two protected tanks in the Ascension merge — and then he left again, days later, forcing Ragie into the spot. Two departures, both at the worst possible moment; the tank crisis that drove the December merge has his fingerprints on it.

bratux.name: Bratux
bratux.html: Bratux was a druid in Ascension with thirty-four guild raids from January through August 2020. Thirteen outside reports predate that tenure and four overlap it. After a long gap, two reports on 16 April 2021 provide the only later trace and do not identify another guild.

broodje.name: Broodje
broodje.html: Broodje was a paladin from the Ninjas roster who appeared three more times after the merger into Dusk. His thirty-four guild raids run from February through early September 2020. Five reports predate the local record and seven overlap it; no later activity appears in the completed search.

brovkin.name: Brovkin
brovkin.html: Brovkin was a druid with one Ninjas raid and nine Dusk raids in the Ahn'Qiraj summer. The Head of Ossirian the Unscarred is his sole documented award. Eight outside reports overlap the local tenure; none appears before it or after it.

buffie.name: Buffie
buffie.html: Buffie was a paladin with eleven Ascension guild raids and one personal PUG from May through July 2020. Twenty outside reports precede the guild tenure, showing a substantial earlier raid history. No report follows the final Ascension appearance.

cappu.name: Cappu
cappu.html: Cappu was a priest in Ascension's early roster. Thirty-seven guild raids survive from October 2019 through March 2020, covering the Molten Core winter and the opening Blackwing Lair weeks. Eight external reports overlap that span; none has been found before it or after it.

carmelia.name: Carmelia
carmelia.html: Carmelia was a priest who raided with Sleep and Dusk, logging 78 raids from 25 March to 22 November 2020, and was in the raid on 19 April 2020 when Zul'Gurub had its first surviving full clear. The loot ledger is one of the deepest in the archive: 48 awards spanning a full run of Prophecy priest gear, two Eye of C'Thun drops, and a Lok'amir il Romathis in November. A June 2020 Discord thread credits Carmelia, alongside Tsakimo, with recruiting the rogue Teo (Ntekapaz) into the guild, part of a real-life friend circle the two shared. Carmelia's last logged raid falls before Naxxramas opened, placing her among the high-attendance veterans who never saw the final tier. Her tribute video sits on Supplier's 2021 "Dusk list," between Glorya's and Wandolina's; no outside report search currently returns results for the name.

castiiel.name: Castiiel
castiiel.html: Castiiel was a warlock in Ascension with twelve guild raids from January through February 2020. Thirteen outside reports predate the local run and one overlaps it. Two reports on 1 March provide the only later activity.

celed.name: Celed
celed.html:
Celed was a rogue from the Ninjas line who held the class-leader seat as a stand-in when Antzi's work schedule bit, and gave it back with the most graceful resignation in the record: "Antzi wants to replace me! We talked about it so much and this is our decision... he knows so much about the game. I'll help going forward." No drama, no politics, a 67-raid resume, and a healer-parse joke at his expense that followed him around one autumn week ("95 parse is worthy of some loot, actually"). The guild ran on its arguers; it also ran on people like Celed, who mostly just showed up and played well.

Celed's final logged Dusk raid was 24 September. The later trail contains sixty-four reports across thirty-eight dates, with Seax present on twenty-seven and Tylph uploading forty-six of the reports. Titles repeat a Tuesday, Thursday and Sunday schedule through Naxxramas. Fifty-three reports across thirty-one dates match Warcraft Logs' historical guild feed for Agile, confirming where that schedule belonged.

chiara.name: Chiara
chiara.html:
Chiara was a hunter in Ninjas and Dusk, completing thirty-two guild raids and one personal PUG between April and September 2020. She joined both the first C'Thun and Ouro kills and the first full Ahn'Qiraj clear. Sixteen outside reports overlap that tenure.

Fourteen later reports resume in October and continue into April 2021. They show that Chiara kept raiding, but the resolved evidence does not establish a destination guild.

chombat.name: Chombat
chombat.html: Chombat was a warrior from the Ascension side of the archive, logging 101 raids from 6 October 2019 to 6 January 2021. Ninety-eight are Ascension sessions and three belong to the joint Dusk–Ascension roster. Chombat attended the first Kel'Thuzad kill on 20 December 2020. Thirty external reports appear during the logged span, but the outside-report evidence shows activity only and does not name a different guild.

cindarella.name: Cindarella
cindarella.html:
Cindarella was a priest whose route touched Sleep once before continuing through Ninjas and Dusk. Her thirty-one guild raids include the first C'Thun and Ouro kills and Dusk's first 9/9 Ahn'Qiraj clear. The loot record preserves The Eye of Divinity and Codex of Renew X.

Eleven outside reports overlap the same summer. None appears after her final Dusk raid on 24 September.

conoflow.name: Conoflow
conoflow.html: Conoflow was a mage whose 95 logged raids ran from 4 December 2019 to 13 September 2020, almost entirely under the Sleep banner with four later Dusk sessions and one personal pug. Conoflow was in the raid for the first Nefarian kill in February 2020 and for the first surviving full Zul'Gurub clear that April. The loot ledger holds 15 awards, among them a Ring of Spell Power, Netherwind Gloves, and a Neltharion's Tear out of Blackwing Lair. The final logged raid falls on the date research into this era marks as the start of the September crisis; no departure message survives, so the record does not show whether that timing was cause or coincidence. A broader report search found one appearance before the logged span and 34 more between 6 October 2020 and 11 May 2021, evidence of continued play rather than a named destination guild.

craxx.name: Craxx
craxx.html: Craxx raided as a hunter for Ascension across 66 raids between 15 January 2020 and 11 April 2021. Ten outside reports predate the run and 21 more overlap it, ending 28 March 2021, with none afterward. No landmark or loot award is documented for Craxx.

crok.name: Crok
crok.html: Crok was a mage with 162 raids in the logs — one of the most-attended players in the whole archive — and the pragmatist in the officer chat. When rosters ran short he suggested filling with pugs and recruiting the good ones ("worked in the past"); when December's crisis meetings ran hot he stayed practical. His DM thread with Artimis spans the guild's whole life, from a February 2020 recruit conversation to three days after the Kel'Thuzad kill. He farmed venom sacks on the night crew, carried the Ring of Spiritual Fervor out of the 12-wipe Horsemen night, and made the jump to Ascension with the rest. During migration week he also relayed alchemy materials between Rockafella and the benched Artimis, keeping the consumables line moving while the guild changed names.

crucibal.name: Crucibal
crucibal.html: Crucibal fought as a warrior for Ascension across 47 raids between 13 May 2020 and 24 March 2021. Thirteen outside reports predate the run and 16 more overlap it, ending the same day as his final logged raid, with none afterward. No landmark or loot award is documented.

cyprinius.name: Cyprinius
cyprinius.html: Cyprinius was a paladin from the Ascension side of the archive, appearing in 93 logged raids between 29 January 2020 and 7 April 2021. Eighty-eight of those raids are Ascension sessions, with four joint Dusk–Ascension raids and one personal pug filling out the total. Cyprinius attended the first joint Naxxramas raid on 9 December 2020 and the first Kel'Thuzad kill, receiving a Band of Unanswered Prayers four days before the clear. Outside the local archive, 32 external reports run from 12 February 2020 to 24 March 2021, documenting activity through the same window rather than a separate guild.

dandy.name: Dandy
dandy.html: Dandy was a warrior in Ascension with thirty-three guild raids from January through June 2020. Seven outside reports precede his local debut and nineteen overlap it, placing the Ascension run inside a broader existing raid history. No later report has been found.

danigerozops.name: Danigerozops
danigerozops.html:
Danigerozops was a warrior who completed seventeen Sleep raids and twenty Dusk raids from June through December 2020. He stayed through Dusk's first guild-only Naxxramas night. The loot archive records seventeen awards, including Quick Strike Ring on his first Sleep night and a run of Molten Core and Blackwing Lair tank gear.

Only three outside reports surround the local tenure, and none comes after his final Dusk appearance. His surviving history is therefore unusually concentrated inside the guild archive.

deadlylock.name: Deadlylock
deadlylock.html: Deadlylock was a warlock who completed fifteen Ninjas raids and six Dusk raids between May and September 2020. He was present for the first C'Thun and Ouro kills. One outside report overlaps the local tenure, and no later appearance has been found.

dejvid.name: Dejvid
dejvid.html: Dejvid was a priest whose twenty-six Sleep raids begin with the first surviving 10/10 Molten Core report and continue into July 2020. One outside report predates that opening by seven weeks. Nothing external overlaps the tenure or follows it, leaving the guild archive as the main record of his Classic raiding.

deliz.name: Deliz
deliz.html:
Deliz was a healer, one of the guild's Norwegian core, and the story's first fairness casualty. In February 2020, a year before anyone had heard of Ascension, he quit WoW over how healers were treated: excluded from best-in-slot rolls while the damage dealers geared, with a disputed Ragnaros neck as the concrete grievance. His exit put a question on the table that the guild never fully answered, and that returned in every later crisis: what does the raid owe the people who keep it alive but never top a meter?

His friendship with Artimis long outlasted his raiding. The messages run from 2019 to 2025 — game recommendations, life updates, and the occasional piece of guild news from the outside, including the December 2020 note that Exclus had deleted the old WoW Classic Discord. In the story of Sleep he is the early warning: the guild's kindest era already contained the argument that would end it.

deltron.name: Deltron
deltron.html: Deltron was a hunter who completed twelve Ninjas raids and eight Dusk raids, including the first C'Thun and Ouro kills. Fifteen outside reports predate his local tenure and ten overlap it. A single report on 2 October is the only later appearance.

demeterra.name: Demeterra
demeterra.html: Demeterra was a priest who crossed from Ninjas into Dusk. Her thirty-eight guild raids include the first C'Thun and Ouro kills on 23 August and the first complete Ahn'Qiraj clear on 3 September. Fourteen outside reports overlap the same June-to-October tenure, but the wider search finds no activity after the final local appearance.

devou.name: Devou
devou.html: Devou was Ascension's warrior officer and the other half of the December negotiation. From the Dusk side of the record he appears as a fair counterpart: the one who offered his own raid spot to a benched Dusk hunter on the first joint night ("thank Devou," Divinestorm insisted, "for understanding how much we wanted a 3rd hunter spot"), and the firm no when a fourth hunter spot was floated. Ascension wanted to stay Ascension and absorb Dusk; he said so openly from day one, which is more than most mergers get. The Ascension side of this story — the KT week, the January era — is still waiting for his version.

divinestorm.name: Divinestorm
divinestorm.html:
Divinestorm appears as a mage in the first surviving complete Molten Core report on 13 November 2019 and ended the following year running the guild. The climb started with an April challenge to mage leader Proctologist. Divinestorm took his case to Artimis, and Rockafella backed him as the person who should have led from the start. The officers made the change. Next came the Dusk channel structure and the loot doctrine, which measured effort through attendance and preparation while leaving the final word with the council. On 2 August he became guild master. The officer chat shows him everywhere. He ran the idol economy item by item, defended benched players one day ("we solved problems for the top raiders, but we haven't solved it for those we bench") and made hard calls the next ("I have no problem making hard calls if needed").

He was also the guild's shock absorber. September 2020 brought a crisis a week: a ninja pull, a rage-quit, an officer resigning live in the channel, a kick war that briefly cost the guild its own tank leader. Divinestorm mediated every one of them, often from work trips, and wrote the member-facing statements afterwards. When Naxxramas exposed the tank roster in December, he concluded overnight that the guild could not continue alone, opened talks with Ascension's officers, and eight days later led the mass migration, planned while everyone hearthed into the raid. The 15/15 Kel'Thuzad kill came four days after that, under his leadership.

The record keeps his personality intact. He bought poison sacs by the hundred and tracked idol distribution person by person. He defended a benched no-name because "the guy worked really hard farming sacs for us", then called himself "the mage who didn't understand hunter loot" while arbitrating a hunter loot fight. He was sworn at in officer chat and told to his face that the leadership was running the guild into the ground, and he answered with the same maddening evenness every time. That evenness is why people trusted him with the December decisions.

It also won people back. Tsakimo quit in July over the rogue loot system, spoke privately with Divinestorm, and returned for Dusk's first AQ40 night as the person updating the loot sheet.

Those decisions are the hard part of his file. The pivot to Ascension saved the raid; 15/15 in fourteen days is the proof. It also ended the guild as a thing of its own and cost it its most loyal bench. Divinestorm took the blame for a botched benching in the same breath as he claimed the authority to bench anyone, which suggests he understood the price better than anyone else at the time.
