djpopz.name: Djpopz
djpopz.html: Djpopz was a warlock in Ninjas with thirty-one guild raids from February through June 2020. Ten outside reports predate the tenure and nineteen overlap it. Twenty more reports return from September through December, showing a substantial later raid history without a confirmed guild name.

docthor.name: Docthor
docthor.html:
Docthor was one of Sleep's original priests, present in the first surviving Molten Core report on 13 November 2019. He completed fifty-six local raid sessions on the priest, while his druid Ursaminor added twelve more. Pnats described him as one of the healers who could almost always be counted on. He covered priest class leadership for Shakey in March and received a Rejuvenating Gem on 29 April.

His final Sleep raid was 14 June. Outside reports begin on 1 July, and Warcraft Logs' historical Exsul guild feed contains forty-six of them across thirty-one dates through December. Officer chat later independently recorded that Docthor and Alcliff were both in Exsul. His wider trail continues into May 2021, ending in the PUG and GDKP circuit where several former Sleep and Dusk names still crossed paths.

dolleboy.name: Dolleboy
dolleboy.html: Dolleboy was a druid whose 70 logged raids, all of them Ascension sessions, span 8 March 2020 to 11 April 2021. No loot award or landmark raid is currently documented for the character. Twenty-five external reports fall inside that span, from 9 March 2020 to 1 March 2021, evidence of activity rather than membership in a named guild.

dragonslay.name: Dragonslay
dragonslay.html:
Dragonslay healed as a priest for Ninjas and, briefly, Dusk: 44 raids between 13 February and 27 August 2020, all but two of them logged under the Ninjas identity.

She was one of Ninjas' class leaders, running raid two's healing assignments, and by April 2020 Dan flagged her as a strong contender for more responsibility even though she was "frustrated with the priests atm," simply because the others weren't buffing and left her doing all the legwork. In July, Snjór said he wanted her "more involved with the management of the guild" as part of a wider push to treat members better, but by August she had stepped back and was taking a break from raid healing. She surfaces once more at the end of September, when Artimis asked Henne whether the person behind a piece of guild drama was "dragonslay" and got a one-word yes, and when Stormcat, asked what stood in the way of salvaging Dusk's two raid teams, answered with just her name. Thirteen outside reports predate her run, 21 overlap it, and one more appears on 3 January 2021.

drekka.name: Drekka
drekka.html: Drekka was a warlock with twelve Ninjas raids and two Dusk appearances between February and August 2020. Twelve outside reports predate his local tenure and eight overlap it. No later activity has been found.

dropos.name: Dropos
dropos.html: Dropos was a priest in Ascension with ten guild raids from January through February 2020. Six outside reports predate the local run and two overlap it. No later appearance has been found.

drágón.name: Drágón
drágón.html: Drágón was a warrior from the Ascension side of the archive, with 83 logged raids between 10 May 2020 and 14 April 2021. Seventy-seven of those are Ascension sessions, five belong to the joint Dusk–Ascension roster, and one is a personal pug. Drágón attended the first joint Naxxramas raid on 9 December 2020 and the first Kel'Thuzad kill eleven days later, though no loot award is currently documented. A broader report search found twelve appearances before the logged span in April 2020, 26 external reports running through it to 11 April 2021, and eleven more from 22 April to 18 May 2021; these establish activity rather than a named destination guild.

dwarfinator.name: Dwarfinator
dwarfinator.html: Dwarfinator was a rogue in Ninjas with fourteen guild raids from May through July 2020. Ten outside reports overlap that short tenure. No report has been found before the local opening or after the final raid.

eboberta.name: Eboberta
eboberta.html: Eboberta was a rogue in Ascension with nineteen guild raids from January through April 2020. Fourteen outside reports predate the local run and seven overlap it. No later appearance has been found.

edomedo.name: Edomedo
edomedo.html: Edomedo was the tank-in-waiting whose exit changed everything. Groomed through November as the contingency ("we have a potential tank lined up"), he preferred tanking to DPS and said so. On the night of December 7th 2020 he told Divinestorm he was quitting the game — and that single conversation set off the chain reaction: no tanks for Four Horsemen, the overnight partnership with Ascension, the twenty-spot cut, and the end of Dusk nine days later. Few players this quiet ever moved a story this much.

elbossos.name: Elbossos
elbossos.html: Elbossos was a hunter in Ninjas with twenty-eight guild raids from March through June 2020. Sixteen outside reports overlap that tenure. Twenty-seven more begin immediately afterward and continue into December, establishing a long later raid history whose guild remains unresolved. One report matches Decimation's historical guild feed, showing that he raided with Decimation at least once without establishing membership.

elderoy.name: Elderoy
elderoy.html: Elderoy was an Ascension priest with thirty-seven guild raids from February through July 2020, plus one personal PUG in the collected archive. Ten external reports overlap that period. No report survives from before the local tenure or after it, leaving a compact record centered on Ascension's Molten Core and Blackwing Lair months.

eldoc.name: Eldoc
eldoc.html:
Eldoc was a warrior from Sleep's opening roster. His twenty-nine local raids begin with the first surviving 10/10 Molten Core report and end on the guild's first Nefarian kill, 23 February 2020. The wider trail resumes four days later, suggesting that the Nefarian night was an endpoint in this archive rather than an endpoint for the player.

Eldoc appears in 121 later reports across forty-two dates. Twenty-three of them form an explicitly titled "Team Storm" series from April through October, first in Molten Core and Blackwing Lair and later in Ahn'Qiraj. The same outside core recurs throughout, but Warcraft Logs has no matching Razorgore guild record under that name. Team Storm is therefore a confirmed raid community, not a confirmed destination guild.

electro.name: Electro
electro.html: Electro was a mage who raided across Sleep, Dusk, and Ascension identities, logging 92 raids from 19 April 2020 to 11 April 2021, and was in the raid for Dusk's first Naxxramas-only night on 6 December 2020. When Divinestorm became mage class leader that May, his roster document records him advocating for Electro's promotion to Raider rank. The loot ledger holds 28 awards, including a Choker of the Fire Lord in July 2020, an Eye of C'Thun that October, and gear spanning Molten Core, Blackwing Lair, and Ahn'Qiraj. Electro's last logged raid is also the final report in the entire local archive, the 11 April 2021 Kel'Thuzad kill, alongside Divinestorm, Fizzi, Zados, Jumanzy, Amarah, and Devou. A separate report search found six external appearances between 25 June 2020 and 31 March 2021, evidence of activity during that span rather than another guild.

esef.name: Esef
esef.html: Esef was a priest in Ascension, with thirty-six guild raids between January and August 2020 plus three personal PUG appearances. His wider record starts two months before the local tenure and adds seven overlapping reports. After the Ascension run, thirteen reports continue into October, documenting continued play without identifying another guild.

eveningshelf.name: Eveningshelf
eveningshelf.html: Eveningshelf was a rogue whose nineteen guild raids crossed Sleep, Ninjas and Dusk. He joined the first C'Thun and Ouro kills and Dusk's first full Ahn'Qiraj clear. One report predates the tenure and four overlap it; a lone appearance in March 2021 is the only later trace.

exclus.name: Exclus
exclus.html:
Exclus came from the Nittedal group as a mage. His holy paladin alt Exclusafk joined a roster whose four paladin spots were all healers. The two characters account for nearly one hundred logged raids between them.

He was also a connector. On 23 October 2019 he vouched for Ragie as "a really good tank," bringing in the player who would anchor the guild's front line.

When Thepaladin lost access to his account, Exclusafk covered the class-leader job from 15 to 22 April 2020. Exclus declined the permanent seat because he was not playing enough, and Randyfist took over. A month later Ragie tried to recruit the paladin alt onto a warrior, creating a brief boundary fight between the tank and paladin leaders. Exclusafk kept raiding through September.

exhopresso.name: Exhopresso
exhopresso.html: Exhopresso fought as a warrior for 62 raids between 13 February and 24 September 2020, 49 of them with Ninjas and 13 after the Dusk merger. He was present for both the first C'Thun and Ouro kills on 23 August and the full Ahn'Qiraj clear eleven days later, a steady attendance record that put him among the guild's more reliable warriors that year even though no loot award is currently documented for him. Eleven outside reports predate the run, 24 overlap it, and one more appears on 5 October 2020 with no destination guild named.

extramedium.name: Extramedium
extramedium.html:
Extramedium was a hunter in Sleep with twenty-two guild raids from November 2019 through April 2020. He joined the first logged Onyxia kill and the first Nefarian kill; Dragonstalker's Breastplate is his documented loot award.

Two reports predate the local record and three overlap it. Six later appearances continue into August without identifying another guild.

fantur.name: Snjór
fantur.html:
Snjór, with Fantur as his warrior alt, came from Iceland with the Ninjas, held their raid leadership, and owned the Dusk Discord server itself. His tank career is the guild's clearest document of what off-tanking actually cost in Classic. Asked to hold Twin Emperors on a second-string gear set, he laid out the math (5,000 gold of Edgemaster's, double consumables, 5,900 health against 5,000-damage strikes) and then delivered the year's most quietly devastating line: "I've been saying this for weeks, and the answer was like, yeah, we can get someone else to do it."

He led Sunday raids, recruited half the server's strays, took responsibility for things that weren't his fault ("I told them to direct their anger at me"), and became the center of the era's worst day when Yeat kicked him on 30 September. Henne said someone then reinvited him and that he, or his alt, kicked her; his later account disputed the surrounding blame. The archive establishes the opening kick and the restriction of kick powers that followed, but not the full sequence or authorization. His summary of guild philosophy outlived all of it: "the mentality we set in Ninjas was always entertainment before some purple pixels."

On 1 October Luivi wrote that Missdotty had told him Snjór joined Agile. The next message separated the fate of his warrior: "No idea if Fantur stays or leaves." The logs complete that small split ending. Snjór's outside reports begin on 29 September, while Fantur continued raiding with Dusk through 21 October.

fatale.name: Fatale
fatale.html: Fatale raided as a warrior for Ascension 52 times between 8 January and 16 September 2020, one of those a personal PUG. One outside report predates the run, 19 overlap it, and five more continue from late September 2020 into May 2021 without naming a destination guild. No landmark or loot award is documented.

ferrua.name: Ferrua
ferrua.html:
Ferrua was a warlock from the Ninjas side with a talent for being the adult in the room. He is the officer whose loot judgment aged best ("turns out Ferrua was right not to give Mika the Rejuv Gem," Luivi conceded months later) and the one who ran healer loot on zero notice the day Orish quit. "Does this mean I decide healer loot today?" he asked. He did it well enough that nobody complained, which in this guild counts as a standing ovation.

His interventions were short and usually decisive: on rage-quitting ("imagine if ten people rage quit, we have no raid"), on second chances, and in defence of Divinestorm when criticism turned personal. He argued for diverse raid comps on principle. "Imagine if we only had warriors and paladins. That would suck."

filippoberio.name: Filippoberio
filippoberio.html: Filippoberio was a warrior with three Ninjas raids and eight Dusk raids in the summer of 2020. He joined the first C'Thun and Ouro kills. Six outside reports predate the local tenure and nine overlap it; no later appearance has been found.

fingerlickin.name: Fingerlickin
fingerlickin.html: Fingerlickin was a rogue in Ascension's long early roster. Thirty-four guild raids stretch from October 2019 into September 2020, with one personal PUG also preserved locally. Eighteen outside reports overlap the same span. No report has been found before the local opening or after the final appearance.

fizzi.name: Fizzi
fizzi.html:
Fizzi was a warrior who treated raid rosters like an engineering problem. By late 2020 he was the Dusk officer doing the unglamorous math: how many hunter spots a merged raid could carry, which classes were oversubscribed, who could tank Four Horsemen if Boxya disappeared again (he kept Edomedo warm as the contingency). When the December merge happened, he was one of the two tanks Dusk protected in the first brutal cut. He had earned it; he'd tanked C'Thun with Glory just weeks earlier.

His philosophy was stated plainly in the December debates: comp plus parse — with limited spots you bring the players who perform, and "bench decisions… I have no problem making hard calls if needed." But the same person argued for alt-and-member loot parity in November, defended benched players' access to gear, and did the tedious work of maintaining signup tabs and week-three spreadsheets that fairness actually runs on.

He was in the first Four Horsemen kill and the Kel'Thuzad clear, and carried on into Ascension's farm era — one of the people whose December choices the story judges gently, because the archive shows how much thought went into them.

flameboy.name: Flameboy
flameboy.html: Flameboy was a mage from the Ascension side of the archive, with 107 logged raids between 15 January 2020 and 11 April 2021. The total includes 101 Ascension raids, five joint Dusk–Ascension sessions, and one personal pug. Flameboy attended the first joint Naxxramas raid and the first Kel'Thuzad kill. Thirteen outside reports predate the logged span and 21 external reports fall within it; they document activity but not membership in another guild.

flyx.name: Flyx
flyx.html: Flyx was a rogue whose 87 raids ran from 17 May 2020 to 11 April 2021 across Sleep, Dusk, and Ascension, present for all three Naxxramas landmarks: the Dusk-only opening, the first joint Dusk–Ascension raid, and the Kel'Thuzad kill. A July 2020 rogue attendance snapshot put Flyx at 100 percent among seven rogue spots, ahead of Pricelez, Tsakimo, and Reiner at 80 percent each. The 27 recorded loot awards include Bloodfang armor pieces, a Drake Fang Talisman, and the Phylactery of Kel'Thuzad from the final clear. Fifteen external reports fall inside the logged span, from 18 June 2020 to 24 March 2021, with two more shortly after; they show continued activity, not a different guild. Supplier's 2021 "Dusk list" tribute video for Flyx sits between Rockafella's and the closing set for Rakaiah, Teo, and Tsakimo.

fnar.name: Fnar
fnar.html: Fnar was a rogue associated primarily with Ascension, appearing in 106 logged raids from 4 December 2019 to 14 April 2021. The count includes 102 Ascension sessions, three joint Dusk–Ascension raids, and one personal pug. Fnar was present for the first joint Naxxramas raid on 9 December 2020. The outside-report history contains five reports before the span, 29 external reports during it, and twelve afterward, evidence of activity rather than membership in a named guild.

fnats.name: Fnats
fnats.html:
Fnats was a restoration druid from the Nittedal circle and the first voice in the whole archive: "Er du i queue?", sent from the launch-day line on 27 August 2019 while his druid was level 10. He and Artimis had been gaming together long before Classic, and kept at it long after: League, Valorant, Tarkov, Halo, whatever was going that month.

In the guild he was one of the two best healers on the roster and the man who fought hardest to make healing loot fair. He spent two months trying to get the Rejuvenating Gem priority settled and eight days waiting for an answer about the healing-officer role. On 18 March 2020, Shakey won the first gem roll, Artimis finally offered Fnats the officer role the same evening, and Fnats took an exam break from the game instead. He left without bitterness and with the most quoted line a guild leader ever received: "as guild leader, you unfortunately stand in the crossfire." His deeper argument outlived the night: the people deciding healer loot were people who would never play a healer.

foreskins.name: Foreskins
foreskins.html: Foreskins was a hunter in Ascension with sixteen guild raids from April through July 2020. Eight outside reports predate his local arrival. Seven later appearances return between December and April 2021, but they do not establish a destination guild.

freelong.name: Freelong
freelong.html: Freelong raided as a mage for Ascension across 52 raids between 15 January 2020 and 31 March 2021. Eight outside reports predate the run and 17 more overlap it, ending 23 March 2021, with none afterward. No landmark or loot award is documented.

freezir.name: Freezir
freezir.html:
Freezir was a warrior with fifteen Ascension guild raids and eight personal PUGs spread across more than a year. His wider history dwarfs that local record: ninety-eight external reports overlap the same span, with two more before it.

Nine reports continue after the final Ascension appearance into May 2021. They document further activity but do not establish a destination guild.

frieda.name: Frieda
frieda.html: Frieda was a hunter in Ascension, logging thirty-seven guild raids between November 2019 and July 2020. Seven external reports overlap that tenure. A single later appearance on 16 November is the only activity found afterward, too little to identify a new raid community or guild.

frostycore.name: Frostycore
frostycore.html: Frostycore was a mage in Ascension's opening roster, completing fourteen guild raids from October through December 2019. Two external reports overlap the tenure. No activity has been found before it or after it.

fruddan.name: Fruddan
fruddan.html: Fruddan was a rogue on Sleep's original surviving roster. His ten guild raids begin with the first complete Molten Core report in November 2019 and end the following month. No outside report appears in the completed search.

galidia.name: Galidia
galidia.html:
Galidia was a warrior from the Nittedal circle and the recipient of the first loot award in the entire workbook: Bracelets of Wrath, Blackwing Lair, 25 March 2020, row one of the ledger everything on this site's loot pages descends from. He raided through the Sleep spring as one of the dependable middle of the roster, the kind of player the officer chat only mentions when a tank is needed on short notice ("I can ask Galidia or Naru to tank, they have the gear").

The friendship outlasted the guild by years. The same DM thread that covers raid signups in 2020 is, by 2025, Artimis explaining index funds and stock picks. Nittedal threads don't really end; they just change topics.

gallithian.name: Gallithian
gallithian.html: Gallithian was a mage whose eleven guild raids include one Sleep appearance and ten with Ninjas. Three outside reports predate that tenure and five overlap it. One final appearance on 25 August is the only later trace.

gambica.name: Gambica
gambica.html: Gambica was a priest in Ascension with thirty-one guild raids from February through July 2020. Sixteen outside reports predate that run and twenty-nine overlap it, evidence of an extensive parallel raid history. No report has been found after the last Ascension appearance.

gamdar.name: Gamdar
gamdar.html: Gamdar was a mage in Ascension's original roster with sixteen guild raids from October through December 2019. Two outside reports overlap that tenure. Seventy later reports continue through June 2020, documenting an extensive second chapter without a confirmed guild name.

ganknor.name: Ganknor
ganknor.html:
Ganknor was a rogue in Ascension's Naxxramas roster. Twenty-four Ascension raids and two joint nights with Dusk form the guild record, alongside two personal PUGs. He joined the first Kel'Thuzad kill and received Boots of Displacement plus two desecrated armor tokens that night.

Forty-one outside reports overlap the local tenure. One final appearance on 21 April 2021 follows it, without establishing a destination.

ganondrake.name: Ganondrake
ganondrake.html: Ganondrake was a paladin in Ascension's opening roster with twelve guild raids from October through December 2019. Three outside reports overlap the tenure. No activity has been found before it or after it.

geniep.name: Geniep
geniep.html: Geniep was a rogue with ten Ascension guild raids and one personal PUG between May and November 2020. Three outside reports predate the guild tenure and four overlap it. Fifteen later reports continue from October through late November without identifying a destination guild.

gheynor.name: Gheynor
gheynor.html: Gheynor was a hunter in Ascension's later roster. Twenty-nine Ascension raids and three joint nights with Dusk form his guild record, including the first joint Naxxramas raid on 9 December. One personal PUG is also preserved. Sixteen outside reports overlap the tenure, but none follows the final local appearance in April 2021.

gibford.name: Gibford
gibford.html:
Gibford was a priest who crossed from Ninjas into Dusk. His twenty-seven guild raids include Dusk's first full Ahn'Qiraj clear. Ten outside reports predate the local tenure and thirteen overlap it.

The later history is much larger: forty-eight reports from September 2020 through March 2021. They prove sustained raiding but do not currently name a destination guild.

gimpara.name: Gimpara
gimpara.html:
Gimpara was a rogue in Sleep with twenty-nine guild raids and one personal PUG from April through August 2020. He joined the first surviving complete Zul'Gurub clear, and twelve documented awards include Quick Strike Ring and several early rogue set pieces.

Two outside reports overlap his tenure. One isolated appearance on 8 May 2021 is the only later trace and does not establish a destination.

glory.name: Glory
glory.html:
Glory appears in the first surviving complete Molten Core report on 13 November 2019. His recruitment was almost accidental: Artimis mistook him for someone else and had already mailed him a cloak before anyone caught the mix-up. He stayed for 159 local raids. He was a protection warrior and a blacksmith good enough to forge Thepaladin's Sulfuron Hammer in March, then five of the six Radiant pieces for the Naxxramas frost-resistance push. By December 2020 he owned a completed Thunderfury, one of very few in the guild.

He asked for very little back. As early as March 2020 he was arguing for nothing more than a fair system, where effort at the bottom of the meters got the same respect as parses at the top. He tanked C'Thun for Dusk as late as 25 November. Then the December merge with Ascension cut the roster to twenty spots, and Glory never got a single Four Horsemen pull. Not one of the twelve wipes on December 13th. On the 14th, at 14:21, he told Artimis the guild master had promised him a spot that evening; at 19:42 the Horsemen died on the night's first pull with forty other names in the log. He heard the strategy briefing from the bench.

The officers had reached a private verdict that same day: a year and a half of trial, not improved, not good enough. Nobody said it to his face. When he asked Artimis directly who had blocked him, Artimis refused to name names, and the answer stayed buried in the archive for five years. Artimis had written his own strike letter that same morning, asking more or less the question Glory's whole December asked: what does a guild owe the loyal? Neither of them got an answer.

Two days later, on the evening the guild mass-migrated into Ascension, Glory left. "Better to go during the change," he said; the guild had been his home, and a spot every other week would have been enough to keep him. Within a week he was tanking Four Horsemen for another guild, in the deep Protection spec he had respecced to on the afternoon Dusk one-shot the fight without him. Invited back after the 15/15 clear, he initially declined; he couldn't abandon the people who had given him a spot. Yet his story in the logs continued. Glory returned for four Ascension raids in 2021 and tanked Kel'Thuzad on 11 April, finally getting his own clear in the last full raid the local archive records. His last word in the message archive, from 2022: not playing WoW any more, for now.

glorya.name: Glorya
glorya.html:
Glorya was a priest healer from the Nittedal circle whose name caused two years of clerical confusion with the warrior Glory, a coincidence the archive has to untangle on nearly every page. The two could hardly have had more different Decembers: while Glory watched the Four Horsemen progression from the bench, Glorya healed it. He is in the roster of the first kill on December 14th and stayed for the full Kel'Thuzad clear.

Dusk's healing was its export product, and Glorya was part of the core that made the merge attractive to Ascension in the first place. He was the kind of steady presence who shows up in the logs far more often than in the drama. When raids ran late or short-handed, Glorya arriving "potentially a little bit late" with Pnats was a recurring line in the healer logistics. His tribute video sits on Supplier's 2021 "Dusk list," between Shakey's and Carmelia's.

glumanda.name: Glumanda
glumanda.html:
Glumanda healed as a paladin for 40 raids between 28 June and 23 November 2020, 23 with Dusk and 14 with Sleep, and was in the roster for the 9/9 Ahn'Qiraj clear on 3 September. Three personal PUGs complete the 40-raid total. Ten loot awards, including a run of Judgement tier pieces, tracked a healer the guild worked hard to keep scheduled.

His university timetable kept forcing the issue. At the end of August 2020 he told Stormcat he could no longer make Wednesday raids because of a late class, prompting officers to look for a paladin willing to swap across from Thursday; by November, still unable to fix the conflict, he left the guild alongside his friend Neferti. Trenfentson called the loss "a fair loss on wednesdays, he's a really good healer," and Stormcat agreed it was "kinda expected" once university work made Wednesdays impossible. Three outside reports predate his run, four overlap it, and two more appear in the same November week he departed.

gnogaine.name: Gnogaine
gnogaine.html: Gnogaine was a mage with seventeen Dusk raids and two personal PUGs during the autumn of 2020. Seven awards include Firemaw's Clutch and Ringo's Blizzard Boots. Twenty reports predate his local arrival, while nine later reports continue into November without identifying a destination guild.

grindo.name: Grindo
grindo.html: Grindo was a mage in Ninjas with nineteen guild raids from April through July 2020. One outside report predates the tenure and sixteen overlap it. Seventeen later reports continue from August into April 2021, documenting continued play without a confirmed guild destination.

gwyniael.name: Gwyniael
gwyniael.html:
Gwyniael healed as a druid for 54 raids between 25 March 2020 and 20 January 2021, nearly all of them (49) with Sleep, and was in the raid for the first full Zul'Gurub clear on 19 April. Twenty-four loot awards, more than almost anyone else in this batch, tracked her through Molten Core, Blackwing Lair and Zul'Gurub drops that spring and summer.

Artimis asked Luivi in early April whether they should make her a full raider healer now that Sleep had an open druid slot; three weeks later, during the second raid team's session on 27 April, she dropped offline partway through, leaving only three healers up. Artimis told Ragie afterward that her disconnect hadn't helped a night already strained by other players' struggles. No outside reports exist before, during, or after her run, so nothing here indicates what she did once she stopped appearing in the archive.

hadara.name: Hadara
hadara.html:
Hadara was a paladin who logged twenty-three Ascension guild raids and eight personal PUGs between April 2020 and April 2021. Thirty-seven external reports overlap that long span. Six more continue into May, including the late PUG and GDKP circuit where former Sleep and Dusk names still appeared together.

Those shared reports document continued activity, not a named destination guild.

hayze.name: Hayze
hayze.html: Hayze was a warrior in Ascension with ten guild raids spread from November 2019 through June 2020. One outside report predates the tenure and one overlaps its final date. No later activity has been found.

hedara.name: Hedara
hedara.html: Hedara was Ascension's druid officer, the second name Divinestorm gave Dusk when the December partnership formed. The archive holds less of him than his role deserves: a healer in the first Four Horsemen kill and the Kel'Thuzad clear, a short friendly DM with Artimis about whether they'd met before ("You're from Norway, right? Your voice is familiar"), and a place in every joint-raid roster through the clear. Like Devou, he is a door this story hasn't opened yet — the Ascension officer chat from December would answer questions this archive can only pose.

hefners.name: Hefners
hefners.html: Hefners was a rogue in Ascension with thirty-two guild raids from January through August 2020. Three outside reports predate that run and fifteen overlap it. The wider search ends with the local tenure and supplies no later destination.

helakion.name: Helakion
helakion.html: Helakion was a warlock whose 75 logged raids, all of them Ascension sessions, span 6 October 2019 to 2 September 2020. The archive documents no landmark raid or loot award for the character. Nineteen external reports fall inside that span, from 13 November 2019 to 23 August 2020, evidence of activity rather than membership in a named guild.

helbred.name: Helbred
helbred.html: Helbred was a priest in Ascension's opening roster with thirteen guild raids from November through December 2019. Two outside reports overlap the tenure and nine more continue into February 2020.

henne.name: Henne
henne.html:
Henne (Linda) came over from the Ninjas side and was one of the voices that bridged the two cultures. Her place in the story is collateral damage from the strangest day of the Dusk era: on September 30th 2020, Yeat kicked Snjór. Henne said someone then reinvited Snjór and that he, or his alt, kicked her; Snjór's later account disputed the surrounding blame. The protest gquits that followed nearly took the guild apart. Artimis's first message to her that afternoon opens one of the archive's DM threads: let's find out what happened and find a fair solution.

She was restored along with everyone else once Divinestorm untangled the mess, and the incident forced the reform that outlived it: kick rights were restricted, and "if you don't have time to explain, you should not have time to kick people" became guild doctrine. Few players did less to deserve their place in the drama, which is why her name is on the reform.

Henne's last logged Dusk raid was 18 October. Her later history contains seventy-nine reports across thirty-three dates, with GDKP and PUG titles under several uploaders. Katdrovrsn and Mikadrovrsn each share seven of those dates, while Ulfhild shares six. Nine reports across seven dates match Decimation's historical guild feed, showing that she raided with Decimation as well as maintaining contact with the old circle.

herberd.name: Herberd
herberd.html: Herberd was a priest whose 74 logged raids, all of them Ascension sessions, span 6 October 2019 to 18 October 2020. Neither a landmark raid nor a loot award is currently recorded for the character. Twenty external reports fall inside that span, from 12 February to 28 September 2020, evidence of activity rather than membership in a named guild.

hex.name: Hex
hex.html: Hex was a druid in Ascension with twenty-six guild raids and one personal PUG from April through July 2020. Nine outside reports predate the local record and eight overlap it. No later appearance has been found.

hilts.name: Hilts
hilts.html: Hilts and the confirmed alt Hiltsey were priests with 154 alt-aware logged raids, from the first logged raid on 6 October 2019 to the last on 14 April 2021. The record is overwhelmingly from the Ascension side of the wider archive: 146 Ascension sessions, four joint Dusk–Ascension raids, and four personal pugs. Hilts attended the first joint Naxxramas raid on 9 December 2020 and the first Kel'Thuzad kill eleven days later. Across the two character names, the Destiny classification totals three before-tenure reports, forty external-during-tenure reports, and eight after-tenure reports; those reports establish activity, not guild membership.

hiltsey.name: Hilts
hiltsey.html: Hilts and the confirmed alt Hiltsey were priests with 154 alt-aware logged raids, from the first logged raid on 6 October 2019 to the last on 14 April 2021. The record is overwhelmingly from the Ascension side of the wider archive: 146 Ascension sessions, four joint Dusk–Ascension raids, and four personal pugs. Hilts attended the first joint Naxxramas raid on 9 December 2020 and the first Kel'Thuzad kill eleven days later. Across the two character names, the Destiny classification totals three before-tenure reports, forty external-during-tenure reports, and eight after-tenure reports; those reports establish activity, not guild membership.

hobbelone.name: Hobbelone
hobbelone.html: Hobbelone was a mage with sixteen Ascension guild raids and one personal PUG between January and August 2020. Three outside reports overlap the tenure. Eleven later reports continue into late August, but no destination guild is identified.

holyhans.name: Holyhans
holyhans.html: Holyhans was a paladin with eleven Ascension guild raids and three personal PUGs from June through September 2020. Nine reports predate that local window and three overlap it. One appearance in November is the only later trace.

holyshule.name: Holyshule
holyshule.html:
Holyshule was a paladin in Sleep with twenty-eight guild raids from April through June 2020. Twenty documented awards chart a rapid Molten Core and Blackwing Lair gearing run, beginning with Lawbringer Boots, Flamewaker Legplates and Malistar's Defender.

The completed wider search finds no outside report at all. His surviving history is contained entirely in the local archive.

hotzz.name: Hotzz
hotzz.html: Hotzz was a priest with ten Ascension guild raids and one personal PUG during the summer of 2020. Six outside reports predate the local tenure and four overlap it. No later appearance has been found.

hydara.name: Hydara
hydara.html:
Hydara healed as a druid for 46 raids between 13 February and 24 September 2020, 38 with Ninjas and eight after the Dusk merger, and was in the raid for the 9/9 Ahn'Qiraj clear on 3 September.

Officers debated his reliability in both directions. In June 2020, when a Tier 2 boots drop went to Amarah instead of him, Ferrua justified it by saying "Hydara has been slacking..., Amarah is always showing up," but a month later Snjór put him forward as "our best option for a healing leader" among the resto druid group that also included Amarah, Shaoxin and Tokir. That same July, it was Hydara who asked that Amarah and Shao be the ones to sit out a raid when the healing roster ran even. Twelve outside reports predate his run, 13 overlap it, and 11 more continue from October through late November 2020, with no destination guild named.

hyúna.name: Hyúna
hyúna.html: Hyúna was a paladin in Ascension with twenty-six guild raids and two personal PUGs between April and September 2020. Twenty-three external reports overlap that period, but none appears before the local opening or after the final recorded raid.

ifly.name: Ifly
ifly.html: Ifly raided as a rogue for Ascension, logging 83 raids between 6 October 2019 and 22 November 2020, all but one of them Ascension sessions and the remainder a personal pug. The archive currently holds neither a landmark raid nor a loot award for the character. A wider report search found no appearances before the logged span, 30 external reports running from 13 November 2019 to 11 November 2020, and five more in the final week of that window; these show continued activity rather than a named guild.

ihide.name: Ihide
ihide.html: Ihide raided as a rogue for Ascension, 69 raids between 15 January 2020 and 7 April 2021. Twelve outside reports precede the run, 38 overlap it, and ten more continue from 18 April through 16 May 2021; none of them name a destination guild. No landmark or loot award is currently documented for Ihide.

ilove.name: Ilove
ilove.html:
Ilove raided as a warrior first in Ascension, then in Dusk, then in both together as the guilds worked jointly toward Naxxramas: 22 raids in Ascension, 19 in Dusk, three in joint Dusk-Ascension raids, and five personal PUGs, for 49 total between 13 September 2020 and 11 April 2021. He was there for the first Dusk-only Naxxramas raid on 6 December, the first joint Dusk-Ascension Naxxramas raid three days later, and the Kel'Thuzad kill on 20 December, and collected ten loot awards along the way including Crul'shorukh, Edge of Chaos.

Officers used him as their example of a reliable fill-in: Divinestorm cited him in November 2020 as a raider "coming... with WBs and consumes" whenever the guild was short on warriors, and during that month's C'Thun fight he and Tsakimo were the only two in their group to survive the first eye beam because they held their spot while a nearby rogue drifted out of position. Attendance didn't protect him from the bench, though: by mid-December he lost his spot to a warrior with four, which drew a frustrated private message from Artimis comparing the two players' matching boss DPS. Nineteen outside reports overlap his run and six more continue into May 2021 without naming a destination guild.

imlok.name: Imlok
imlok.html: Imlok raided as a warlock for Ascension across 42 raids between 22 March 2020 and 11 January 2021, four of them personal PUGs. Fourteen outside reports overlap the run and 19 more continue from August 2020 into May 2021, without naming a destination guild. No landmark or loot award is documented.

immohalx.name: Immohalx
immohalx.html: Immohalx was a priest with seventeen Ascension guild raids and one personal PUG from January through May 2020. Seventeen outside reports predate that window and twenty-five overlap it. Three later appearances continue into August without establishing another guild.

instant.name: Instant
instant.html: Instant was a paladin whose early guild path includes five Ascension raids and eighteen Sleep raids. He appears in the first surviving complete Molten Core report and the first logged Onyxia kill in November 2019. No outside Warcraft Logs report appears anywhere in the completed search.

isamu.name: Isamu
isamu.html: Isamu raided as a mage for 40 raids between 20 November 2019 and 22 November 2020, 28 with Sleep and nine after the Dusk merger, plus three personal PUGs. Two loot awards bookend his final months: Netherwind Boots that October and a Band of Forced Concentration on his last logged raid. A single outside report falls during his run, on 27 September 2020, and two more follow in December 2020 and January 2021, with no destination guild named.

itspizzatime.name: Itspizzatime
itspizzatime.html: Itspizzatime was a priest in Ninjas who made one further appearance after the Dusk merger. His twenty-one guild raids span February through August 2020. Seven reports predate that tenure and six overlap it; none appears afterward.

jangera.name: Jangera
jangera.html:
Jangera was the hunter who joined Sleep in June and spent much of the summer PvP ranking. The officers noticed the work even when they disagreed over how loot should reward it. Across twenty-five Sleep and Dusk raid sessions, his awards included Ashkandi and Jom Gabbar. His last local raid was 28 October, when officer chat recorded that he was leaving to run GDKPs. His first later reports, four days afterward, are exactly that.

By 17 December Jangera was raiding with Melon. Warcraft Logs' historical guild feed contains thirty-one of his later reports across twenty-two dates, continuing through Melon's final Classic Naxxramas run on 16 May 2021. His full post-Dusk history is broader, with eighty-eight reports across forty-nine dates, but the Melon sequence is a confirmed guild destination rather than an inferred roster cluster.

jellopy.name: Jellopy
jellopy.html:
Jellopy was the guild's first rogue class leader, running the class through the Molten Core and Onyxia autumn of 2019 with a five-slot raider roster he picked himself. He also wired early Discord webhooks for Artimis, part class leader and part guild tech support.

His 26 logged raids all predate Blackwing Lair. On 4 February 2020 he delegated the job plainly: "Kodf will act as CL and loot council." Three weeks later Artimis asked whether the promotion should become permanent. "Yea for sure, promote the man!" Jellopy replied. He had hoped to do one last raid before announcing his own departure, but never found the time. Most guild history isn't drama. Sometimes the important people just log off.

jerricho.name: Jerricho
jerricho.html: Jerricho was a warrior in Ascension. The archive records thirty-three guild raids and five personal PUGs between January and November 2020. Fourteen outside reports show that he was already active before his local debut, and twenty more run alongside the Ascension tenure. Five final reports continue into late November without establishing a new guild.

jinx.name: Jinx
jinx.html: Jinx was a warlock in Ascension with eleven guild raids from February through April 2020. One outside report predates the local run and nine overlap it. No later activity has been found.

jubii.name: Jubii
jubii.html: Jubii was a rogue in Ascension's opening roster, completing eighteen guild raids from October through December 2019. Three outside reports overlap the tenure and three more follow into January 2020. No broader later trail has been found.

juggalog.name: Juggalog
juggalog.html: Juggalog raided as a warrior for Ascension, logging 79 raids from 15 January to 23 December 2020, 77 of them Ascension sessions and two personal pugs. No landmark raid appears in the record, and no loot award is documented. A wider report search found thirteen appearances before the logged span, between 6 November 2019 and 8 January 2020, and 25 external reports inside it running to 18 November 2020; these establish activity, not a named destination guild.

jumanzy.name: Jumanzy
jumanzy.html:
Jumanzy was a mage whose 150 logged raids stretch from 4 December 2019 to 11 April 2021 across Sleep, Dusk, Ascension, and their joint roster. The count includes 81 Sleep raids, 37 with Dusk, 25 with Ascension, five joint sessions, and two personal pugs. Jumanzy was present for the first Nefarian kill, the first surviving full Zul'Gurub clear, both openings of Naxxramas, and the first Kel'Thuzad kill.

The loot ledger records 37 awards, including Neltharion's Tear, Staff of the Shadow Flame, Mind Quickening Gem, and a Brimstone Staff from Naxxramas. In February 2020, mage leader Procto sought Jumanzy's promotion after writing that the mage had “outshined wackd long time ago”; later records show Divinestorm delegating mage responsibilities to Jumanzy during work travel. After the December clear, a surviving screenshot preserves Jumanzy thanking Artimis for the journey through Sleep, Dusk, and Ascension.

juud.name: Juud
juud.html: Juud was a warrior who crossed from Ninjas into Dusk and Ascension, logging 74 raids from 13 February 2020 to 17 March 2021, split 40 to Ninjas, 18 to Ascension, 11 to Dusk, four joint Dusk–Ascension sessions, and one personal pug. Juud was in the raid for six successive landmarks: the first C'Thun and Ouro kills, the first complete 9/9 Ahn'Qiraj clear, Dusk's Naxxramas opening, the first joint raid, and the Kel'Thuzad kill, receiving Legplates of Carnage on the joint-raid night. Research into the Kel'Thuzad roster singles out Juud and Amarah as the only two former Ninjas players in that final lineup. During the December 2020 roster debate over Naxxramas tank spots, officer Zados named Juud as the pick kept over Artimis and judged the choice harshly in the officer chat. A broader report search found seven appearances before the logged span, between 18 December 2019 and 6 February 2020, and 23 external reports running through it to 3 February 2021, evidence of activity rather than a named guild.

kaasdipje.name: Kaasdipje
kaasdipje.html: Kaasdipje was a warrior in Ninjas who made three later appearances for Dusk. His thirty-one guild raids stretch from March into November 2020. Legguards of the Fallen Crusader, awarded in September, are the sole documented loot entry. Twelve outside reports overlap the tenure and none follows it.

karne.name: Karne
karne.html: Karne was an Ascension hunter with thirty-six guild raids from January through May 2020. Six outside reports precede the local record and thirteen overlap it. The completed search finds no later appearance, so the surviving trail ends with the Ascension tenure.

katdrovrsn.name: Katdrovrsn
katdrovrsn.html: Katdrovrsn was a warrior from the Ninjas line who continued into Dusk, logging 74 raids from 23 February to 23 November 2020, split 55 to Ninjas and 18 to Dusk with one personal pug. Katdrovrsn was in the raid for the first complete 9/9 Ahn'Qiraj clear on 3 September 2020, having received a Manual of Heroic Strike IX from Ruins of Ahn'Qiraj two weeks earlier. Twenty-nine external reports run alongside the logged span, from 23 February to 10 September 2020. The later trail contains 51 reports across 35 dates, with Mikadrovrsn present on 28 and Khazam on 14. Five later reports across five dates match Decimation's historical guild feed, showing that Katdrovrsn raided with Decimation. Five dates also belong to a weekly series titled "Safe Haven BWL," but Warcraft Logs has no matching Razorgore guild record; the evidence supports a named raid community, not confirmed membership.

keri.name: Keri
keri.html: Keri was a mage whose 76 logged raids, every one classified to Ascension, run from 24 November 2019 to 7 December 2020. No documented landmark raid or loot award accompanies the record. A broader report search found two appearances before the logged span, in October and November 2019, and 27 external reports running from 16 February to 18 November 2020, evidence of activity rather than a named guild.

khazam.name: Khazam
khazam.html:
Khazam raided as a mage through both the Ninjas and Dusk chapters of the guild's history: 58 raids with Ninjas, then 12 more after the August 2020 merger, for 70 raids between 16 February and 24 September 2020. He was present for the first C'Thun and Ouro kills on 23 August and the following full Ahn'Qiraj clear on 3 September.

Officers rated him among the guild's best mages, sometimes with visible envy. In July 2020 Bandito complained, half-joking, that "Khazam got everything" from a night's drops and that he had "khazamed his way to all the loot," while Celed named him alongside Snjór as the two top parsers on Chromaggus. By September, once Kolfinna and Snjór stepped back from Thursday raiding, Banamahs listed Khazam as one of the four mages left holding that team together. Five outside reports predate his local run and 29 more overlap it; a further 27 continue from November 2020 into May 2021. Two of those later reports, on two dates, match Decimation's historical guild feed, showing that he sometimes raided with Decimation without establishing membership.

knedlica.name: Knedlica
knedlica.html:
Knedlica was one of the hunters waiting for an Ancient Petrified Leaf in the guild's first winter. His gun was already stronger than Ravna's and Nereb's bows, so Artimis asked whether they could go first. Knedlica agreed, adding his own theorycraft about weapon speed and waiting for the tier pants that would solve his hit chance.

Real life pulled him away in spring 2020, when the pandemic and a local earthquake made raiding impossible. He asked to be moved to an inactive rank and hoped to return for a later phase. It was the kind of departure the early guild handled well: clear and without blame.

kodf.name: Kodf
kodf.html:
Kodf ran the rogues, and for a while he quietly ran much of the guild. Jellopy made him acting rogue leader on 4 February 2020 and endorsed the full promotion twenty days later. Kodf built the loot system his class became famous for, fair enough that months after he left officers were still wishing someone could "do Kodf's system." His officer-chat exchanges with Artimis in March 2020 are the guild's constitutional debates: hunters versus rogues on weapon priority, how much a member who shows up is owed, and whether kindness or performance should decide the marginal raid spot.

He was also the road not taken. When Artimis looked for a successor, Kodf got the first offer to take over Sleep, and he declined. In early July he was already rarely online. His final class-leader work included moving Ntekapaz to daggers and planning a seventh rogue spot. By 9 July he had left for Conviction; Lyvana followed by the 11th, while Kodf's alt remained behind. He left the way he did everything: tidily, with a handover, and he kept helping his old guildmates afterwards.

His fingerprints stayed on the guild long after his name left the roster: the rogue loot queues, the expectation that a class leader actually leads, and a small mystery he'd be amused by. The officers spent the autumn debating "another Kodf" and never quite found one.

kofte.name: Kofte
kofte.html: Kofte raided as a druid for Ascension across 45 raids between 15 January and 28 June 2020, one of them a personal PUG. Nine outside reports predate the run and 19 more overlap it, ending 5 June 2020, with none afterward. No landmark or loot award is documented.

kolfinna.name: Kolfinna
kolfinna.html:
Kolfinna raided as a mage for 47 raids between 20 February and 10 September 2020, 40 of them with Ninjas and seven after the Dusk merger, and was present for the first C'Thun and Ouro kills on 23 August.

He was the kind of player officers were reluctant to bench. On 10 September 2020, weighing a tight mage roster, Banamahs argued for keeping him in despite a late signup because "Kolfinna misses som raids at times but he always makes sure to message me if he can't make it," adding that he'd been improving a lot lately. Eight days later Kolfinna stepped back from Thursday raiding entirely, Banamahs explained, because he was struggling to combine it with work, one of three departures (with Snjór and Arcanefarts) that thinned the Thursday mage team at once. Eighteen outside reports overlap his run, from 23 February to 10 September 2020, with none before or after.

kretin.name: Kretin
kretin.html: Kretin was a mage in Ascension's original recorded roster. Thirty-one guild raids survive from October 2019 through February 2020. Only one external report overlaps that span, and the completed search finds nothing before or after it.

kugel.name: Kugel
kugel.html:
Kugel was the original main tank, the warrior the guild built its first raids around. He recruited Thepaladin, who remembered him as the first person he got to know in Sleep, and received an early Binding of the Windseeker when handing a legendary component to your main tank seemed obviously right. Then, in January 2020, he simply stopped logging in. Thepaladin counted twenty-three days of silence before the officers began asking around. By February the main-tank vacancy was official, and in March Kugel was quietly removed after two months offline.

His disappearance shaped the guild twice over. It handed the tank mantle to Ragie and opened the gearing question that Glory, Zhena, and later Snjór would each live through in turn. And the Binding that left with him became guild doctrine: from then on, legendary priority was tied to reliability and long-term commitment — a rule written, like most guild rules, in response to a specific disappointment. Nobody in the archive ever says where he went.

lanaya.name: Lanaya
lanaya.html: Lanaya was a hunter in Ascension's opening roster, completing seventeen guild raids from October through December 2019. Three outside reports overlap the tenure. Forty-six later reports continue through June 2020, showing extensive activity without a confirmed destination.

letmemaryjan.name: Letmemaryjan
letmemaryjan.html:
Letmemaryjan was a rogue who joined Ninjas through Seax, his real-life friend. Celed introduced him to the officers as prepared and experienced, then worked to find him a Blackwing Lair place. He completed twenty-three Ninjas raids and one Dusk raid between May and August 2020.

Ten outside reports overlap the tenure. No activity has been found after his final local appearance.

lightwel.name: Lightwel
lightwel.html: Lightwel was a paladin in Ascension with twelve guild raids in March and April 2020. Ten outside reports predate the local tenure and five overlap it. One isolated appearance in August is the only later trace.

logen.name: Logen
logen.html: Logen was a paladin in Ninjas with twelve guild raids from April through June 2020. Four outside reports overlap the tenure. No report has been found before the local opening or after the final raid.

luilui.name: Luilui
luilui.html: Luilui was a warrior in Ascension with twenty-three guild raids from April through August 2020. Six reports predate his local arrival and two overlap the tenure. One final appearance on 16 August is the only later trace.

luivi.name: Luivi
luivi.html:
Luivi was the druid class leader whose one decision reshaped the whole story: in July 2020, Sleep offered him the guild-master seat. He turned it down (no time for it) and instead asked his contacts in Ninjas whether they'd consider merging. That conversation became Dusk. It's hard to name a more consequential "no" in the guild's history.

As a leader he ran the druids with visible pride ("Druids, the most civilized Class") and a warm, blunt style that survived translation from his native language into rapid-fire officer-chat English. In the Nayla saga he was the patient center, voting for a last warning while admitting the man exhausted him. When officer arguments overheated he was the one who kept perspective: no one was dying, the content was getting cleared, chill out a bit.

vikka.name: Luivi
vikka.html:

He turned it down (no time for it) and instead asked his contacts in Ninjas whether they'd consider merging. That conversation became Dusk. lyriss.name: Lyriss
lyriss.html:
Lyriss was a rogue in Ascension, with fifty-six local guild raids from February through 7 December 2020. Twelve reports predate that tenure, and another twenty-one overlap it outside the local archive. The record shows a player with an established raid life beyond the reports collected for this project.

Three days after the final Ascension appearance, Lyriss begins a later run of seventy-four reports across fifty-three dates. Zhorax uploaded thirty-six of them, following a stable Naxxramas roster into May 2021; a second set under Aceto Balsamico overlaps through joint-run titles. The continuity is strong, but no source currently supplies a guild name for either group.

lyvana.name: Lyvana
lyvana.html:
Lyvana raided as a warlock for Sleep sixty-one times between 1 March and 29 July 2020, picking up fourteen loot awards including Mish'undare, Circlet of the Mind Flayer, in her final month.

She also did the unglamorous officer work: covering loot sorting and bloodvine requests for Rocka more than once that spring, and crafting soul shard bags for the guild on request. Her departure became a small event. On 11 July, Tsakimo told Artimis that both Lyvana and Kodf had already gquit; two days later Artimis described it to Shakey as the two of them leaving together "to join a new guild that was more hardcore," a move Shakey found more surprising than any other departure that summer because he'd assumed they were "lifers in sleep." Lyvana nevertheless returned for Sleep's Zul'Gurub and Onyxia farm raids on 29 July, which account for the later endpoint in the logs. Seven outside reports follow in July, and 24 more continue from August through early December 2020 without identifying the new guild by name.

mackmanaman.name: Mackmanaman
mackmanaman.html: Mackmanaman was a hunter in Ascension's earliest roster. Twenty guild raids survive from October 2019 through February 2020. One outside report overlaps that span; nothing has been found before it or after it.

maddas.name: Maddas
maddas.html: Maddas was a priest in Ninjas with seventeen guild raids from February through April 2020. Six outside reports predate that tenure and six overlap it. No later appearance has been found.

maevis.name: Maevis
maevis.html: Maevis was a mage in Ascension with twelve guild raids from June through October 2020. One outside report overlaps the tenure. The completed search finds no activity before the local opening or after the final raid.

maffe.name: Maffe
maffe.html: Maffe was a paladin in the Ascension lineage, with 93 logged raids running from 22 January 2020 to 14 April 2021. The record splits into 88 Ascension sessions and five joint Dusk–Ascension raids, with no personal pugs recorded. Maffe was present for the first joint Naxxramas raid and the first Kel'Thuzad kill, taking home a Shield of Condemnation on the clear night. A broader report search found sixteen appearances before the logged span, running from 7 October 2019 to 8 January 2020, and 29 external reports inside it through 12 April 2021; these show continued play, not a named guild.

magaliee.name: Magaliee
magaliee.html: Magaliee was a rogue with ten Dusk raids and two personal PUGs during the autumn of 2020. Three Ahn'Qiraj awards preserve her short gearing trail: Imperial Qiraji Armaments, Vek'lor's Diadem and Qiraji Bindings of Command. One outside report predates her Dusk tenure and one overlaps it. Twenty-one later reports continue from November through 13 December, but they do not identify a destination guild.

mansawtiger.name: Mansawtiger
mansawtiger.html: Mansawtiger was a rogue with eight Ninjas raids and four Dusk raids from June through September 2020. Five outside reports overlap the first month of that tenure. No report appears before the local opening or after the final raid.

mdk.name: Mdk
mdk.html: Mdk raided as a rogue for Ascension across 41 raids between 6 October 2019 and 18 March 2020. Thirteen outside reports overlap the run, from 13 November 2019 to 15 March 2020, with none before or after. No landmark or loot award is documented.

mechar.name: Mechar
mechar.html:
Mechar tanked or DPSed as a warrior for Sleep 63 times between 5 February and 5 July 2020, catching the first Nefarian kill on 23 February and the first full Zul'Gurub clear on 19 April. One personal PUG brings his local total to 64 raids. Twenty loot awards across Molten Core, Onyxia, Zul'Gurub and Blackwing Lair, including the Head of Nefarian, made him one of the best-geared warriors of that stretch.

Officers considered him flexible enough to fill gaps: in April 2020 Artimis suggested to Zypher that Mechar could join the second raid team as a tank when the usual off-tanks were unevenly split between rosters. A month later, pnats privately flagged something odd about a Ragnaros drop that Randy had quickly self-equipped instead of trading, an item pnats believed should have gone to "Mechar/Naru" instead. Two outside reports overlap his run, from 22 February to 22 June 2020, with none before or after.

melic.name: Melic
melic.html:
Melic was a hunter with sixteen Ascension guild raids and five personal PUGs between February and September 2020. Eleven reports predate the guild window and twenty-eight overlap it.

Fourteen later reports continue from October into May 2021. They establish continued play but not a named destination.

menrias.name: Menrias
menrias.html: Menrias was a rogue whose 104 logged raids all belong to the Ascension lineage, beginning on 30 October 2019 and ending on 7 December 2020. The inventory currently records no named landmark attendance or loot award for Menrias. Seventeen external Warcraft Logs reports fall within the same span, but they establish raid activity rather than membership outside Ascension.

messia.name: Messia
messia.html: Messia was a priest in Ascension's earliest recorded months. Thirty-six guild raids span October 2019 through April 2020, while eleven external reports overlap the same period. No report has been found before the local opening or after the final Ascension raid.

mikadrovrsn.name: Mikadrovrsn
mikadrovrsn.html: Mikadrovrsn was a paladin from the Ninjas line who continued into Dusk, logging 76 raids from 23 February to 23 November 2020, split 57 to Ninjas and 17 to Dusk with two personal pugs. Mikadrovrsn was in the raid for the first complete 9/9 Ahn'Qiraj clear on 3 September 2020, though no loot award is currently documented. Twenty-four external reports run alongside the logged span, from 23 February to 6 September 2020. The later trail contains 45 reports across 30 dates, with Katdrovrsn present on 28 and Khazam on 13. Five later reports across five dates match Decimation's historical guild feed, showing that Mikadrovrsn raided with Decimation. Two reports are titled "Safe Haven BWL," while the wider history mixes several PUG and raid communities; none proves formal guild membership.

mikasalord.name: Mikasalord
mikasalord.html: Mikasalord was a priest from the Ascension lineage with 102 logged raids between 15 January 2020 and 11 April 2021. The inventory records 97 Ascension sessions and five joint Dusk–Ascension raids. Mikasalord attended both the first joint Naxxramas raid and the first Kel'Thuzad kill, receiving Desecrated Bindings on 16 December and Resilience of the Scourge on the clear night. The wider probe found twelve reports before this span, 24 external reports during it, and eleven afterward; these are records of activity, not proof of another guild.

mikutron.name: Mikutron
mikutron.html: Mikutron raided as a mage for Ascension thirty-nine times from February through September 2020. Fourteen outside reports predate that run and twenty-one overlap it, showing that the local archive captured only one part of an already active character history. No later report has been found after the final Ascension appearance.

mikutronic.name: Mikutronic
mikutronic.html: Mikutronic was a druid with fourteen Ascension guild raids and one personal PUG from May through August 2020. Four later reports are spread between the final local date and May 2021. They show occasional continued play but no named destination.

missdotty.name: Missdotty
missdotty.html:
Missdotty, Dotty for short and Decretum on Discord, was a warlock, the Thursday team's off-boss tank when a fight demanded one, and the officer chat's investigator-in-chief. When idols went missing from the guild bank pipeline, Dotty traced them mailbox by mailbox ("the investigator!"). When arguments ran to 150 messages, Dotty arrived late, sighed "99% shit, 1% information, as usual," and set up a poll. The Among Us jokes wrote themselves, and Dotty leaned in.

The record also holds a running comedy of mistaken identity: half the guild spent months assuming Missdotty was a woman, a discovery that cost Pnats a genuine crisis ("She's not?" / "I can be, if you want"). Behind the jokes sat a reliable officer, hardline in the Nayla debate, generous in the Tear queue, and the one who kept Discord's machinery of polls and roles and tags actually working.
