moonfeather.html: Moonfeather was a druid in Sleep with twenty guild raids from December 2019 through April 2020. Cenarion Boots are the sole documented loot award. No outside report appears in the completed character search.

morpanos.name: Morpanos
morpanos.html:
Morpanos was a mage in Ascension's closing chapter. Twenty-two Ascension raids and five joint nights with Dusk include the first joint Naxxramas run and the first Kel'Thuzad kill.

His earlier history is enormous beside the local tenure: one hundred reports before his November arrival. Thirteen outside reports overlap it and another thirteen continue into May 2021, but the later group is not named by the resolved evidence.

mounaros.name: Mounaros
mounaros.html:
Mounaros was a warlock in the Dusk-to-Ascension transition. Eight Dusk raids, two joint nights and eleven Ascension raids form his guild record, with three personal PUGs also preserved. He joined Dusk's first guild-only Naxxramas run and the first Kel'Thuzad kill; his awards include a Desecrated Circlet.

Seventy-six reports predate his local arrival and twenty-three overlap the tenure. No report follows the final local appearance.

murvar.name: Murvar
murvar.html: Murvar raided as a mage for Ascension across 48 raids between 12 February and 23 August 2020, one of them a personal PUG. Twenty-eight outside reports overlap the run and one more appears three days after his final logged raid, on 26 August 2020. No landmark or loot award is documented.

mysor.name: Mysor
mysor.html: Mysor was a rogue from the Ascension lineage with 110 logged raids, beginning on 15 January 2020 and ending on 7 April 2021. The total comprises 105 Ascension sessions and all five of the first joint Dusk–Ascension raids. Mysor attended the joint Naxxramas opening and the first Kel'Thuzad kill, then received four Naxxramas armor awards between 13 and 16 December. Outside the local archive, the probe found 17 reports before the span, 51 during it, and eleven after it; those reports indicate activity, not guild membership.

namelessqt.name: Namelessqt
namelessqt.html:
Namelessqt was a warrior in Ascension with eleven guild raids from October through December 2020. The local tenure is a small slice of a much larger history: 126 reports predate it and two overlap it.

Forty-five later reports continue from December into May 2021. They prove sustained raiding but do not currently identify a destination guild.

nanis.name: Nanis
nanis.html:
Nanis fought as a warrior for 67 raids between 5 March and 24 September 2020, split 49 raids in Ninjas and 17 after the Dusk merger, plus one personal PUG, and stood in the raid for both the C'Thun/Ouro kills on 23 August and the full Ahn'Qiraj clear on 3 September.

Loot officers repeatedly used him as the example of a raider who didn't grab for gear: in July 2020 Bandito noted "Nanis would have gotten axes had he wanted to" but let others take priority, and a month earlier had argued Nanis deserved a contested Vis'kag drop over other contenders. In August, Bandito offered him the warrior class-leader role and stepped back himself, prompting Dan to write that Nanis "has always been more of a back bench player, fantastic warrior and always motivated in raids," glad to see him take on officer responsibility. Three outside reports precede the run, 20 overlap it, and 40 more continue from late September through 9 December 2020.

nanul.name: Nanul
nanul.html: Nanul was a druid in Ascension with ten guild raids during April and May 2020. One outside report predates the local run and three overlap it. No later appearance has been found.

naru.name: Naru
naru.html: Naru was a warrior with 116 logged raids from 15 January to 6 December 2020, chiefly across Sleep and Dusk. Naru attended Sleep's first Nefarian kill and Dusk's first Naxxramas raid, which was also the last logged appearance in the archive. Private officer records name Naru among the warriors considered for development as alternative tanks. The loot ledger contains 28 awards, including Ashkandi, Lifegiving Gem, Styleen's Impeding Scarab, Maladath, and several Wrath pieces.

nayla.name: Nayla
nayla.html:
Nayla was a feral druid and off-tank whose two years in the guild produced more officer-chat discussion than almost anyone else's. He was generous with his time, always available, always signed, and famously difficult to pin down: conversations relayed through him had a way of arriving changed, to the point where officers joked they needed screenshots.

The warning signs predated Dusk. In July 2020 an officer was already explaining a dispute with "Nayla has a feud with many people." The same week Nayla bought a Scarlet Kris from the guild bank, a small reminder that the ordinary guild machinery kept running around the conflict.

The autumn of 2020 is where his file thickens. An apparent ninja pull in AQ20 turned out, on investigation, to be a misunderstanding (he had been teleported onto the boss while trying to hearth out), but it landed on top of older friction and split the officers between removal and mercy. They debated for a night; one called his behavior toxic, another called him loyalty you can't buy. The verdict was one final chance, framed as a fresh start for the new guild. He lost his tank spot soon after, flirted with rerolling rogue, and was still being proposed for raider rank as late as October. Then on 25 November he left in a burst of drama, messaging guild members that their leader had committed a "last desperate act of evilness". What that act was, the archive still doesn't record. On 20 November, officer chat recorded that he had joined Inheritance. His first outside reports begin six days later, alongside a new audience on the realm Discord.

The record is unusually rich on how people experienced him. His class leader defended him as "a soul whose intentions are good" in the same message as admitting he was exhausting. Officers learned to talk to him only in pairs, so there would be a witness. When he told one officer he had "lost his tanking spot", the officer who supposedly took it away had no idea what he was talking about — a small scene that explains his whole file.

And yet the guild kept almost keeping him. He survived a removal announcement, earned back a bench slot, and was seriously proposed for promotion six weeks before the end. Whatever his parting accusation meant, within two weeks he was raiding elsewhere, loudly himself on the realm Discord. His will to play was never the problem.

The completed later history sharpens that ending. Nayla appears in eighty-two reports across fifty-four dates; the first stable roster progressed through Naxxramas and recorded 15/15 on 18 January 2021, then titled its 8 April run as the last. Later "Beer Garden" farm reports use a different roster. The contemporary officer message supplies the Inheritance name; the reports confirm sustained raiding but do not carry the guild name themselves.

neptun.name: Neptun
neptun.html: Neptun was Ragie's girlfriend and part of the Nittedal circle. She was a mage in the December core, one of the names the officers refused to cut when the merge math got brutal ("we don't want to cut Neptun or Jumanzy or Electro — all three of them in a good raid team will perform very well"), and part of the first Four Horsemen kill and the Kel'Thuzad clear.

nereb.name: Nereb
nereb.html: Nereb was the third hunter in the rotation that defined December — the agreement by which he, Artimis and Zados took turns sitting out when the merged raid allowed the class only a few spots. He'd been there from the early days. In November 2019 Knedlica agreed that Nereb and Ravna, whose bows were weaker, should receive Rhok'delar leaves before him. Nereb was in the first Four Horsemen kill on the night both his rotation partners watched from outside. In the debates about hunter spots he was one of the three names even the hardliners agreed had to be protected: "Artimis is a special case, so is Zados and Nereb."

nikai.name: Nikai
nikai.html: Nikai was a druid from the Ascension side of the archive, with 75 logged raids between 15 January and 20 December 2020. Seventy-one of those raids are Ascension sessions, three belong to the joint Dusk–Ascension roster, and one is a personal pug. Nikai attended the first joint Naxxramas raid and the first Kel'Thuzad kill, receiving Desecrated Handguards a week before the clear. A wider report search found seven appearances before the logged span, between 11 December 2019 and 8 January 2020, and 21 external reports inside it running to 18 November 2020; these establish activity, not a named destination guild.

nikaido.name: Nikaido
nikaido.html: Nikaido was a priest associated primarily with Ascension, appearing in 110 logged raids between 15 January 2020 and 14 April 2021. The inventory records 105 Ascension raids, four joint Dusk–Ascension sessions, and one personal pug. Nikaido attended the first Kel'Thuzad kill and received Desecrated Leggings, Spire of Twilight, and Ring of Faith during the final progression week. The broader report history contains 16 reports before this span, 27 external reports during it, and nine afterward, none of which by itself identifies a guild.

nonstickpan.name: Nonstickpan
nonstickpan.html: Nonstickpan was a rogue with ten Ascension guild raids and four personal PUGs between June and October 2020. One outside report predates the guild tenure and seventeen overlap it. A final appearance on 25 October is the only later trace.

noxou.name: Noxou
noxou.html:
Noxou raided as a warlock for 47 raids between 16 February and 24 September 2020, 39 with Ninjas and eight after the Dusk merger, catching both the first C'Thun and Ouro kills on 23 August and the full Ahn'Qiraj clear on 3 September.

He wasn't without friction. In May 2020, Snjór vented in the officer chat about Noxou and itspizzatime complaining that the loot council wasn't working for them, pointing out neither had shown up for Molten Core in months while letting others carry the raid. By August, though, he was valued enough as a package: Dan noted that Noxou, Broodje and Yeat were real-life friends who wanted to keep raiding together, complicating any plan to move a paladin between the Wednesday and Thursday teams. Seven outside reports predate his run, 13 overlap it, and one more appears on 29 September 2020.

ntekapaz.name: Ntekapaz
ntekapaz.html:
Ntekapaz joined Sleep through Tsakimo and Carmelia on 28 June 2020. The rogue was only five days old but already attuned. He wanted a team worth staying with. When told that alts could receive loot before initiates, he objected once, then gave the line that explains why he fit: "I dont mind wasting a few gear runs in order to have a nice raidingteam."

Kodf moved him to daggers and funnelled the available drops his way, planning a seventh rogue spot even as he prepared to leave. Ntekapaz then became the clearest witness to the three-week Twx experiment. He reported the self-awarded tier pieces and challenged performance loot with the logs. His answer was always Kodf's round-robin system. Other rogues left. Ntekapaz stayed because he believed the problem could be fixed.

His warrior Malakor later joined the same November pug as Tsakimo and Artimis, proof that the friendships survived the loot revolt. He was also leveling the summon bot Ntekabot when the thread ends.

nutellâ.name: Nutellâ
nutellâ.html:
Nutellâ was a warlock in Ascension's early Molten Core roster. Eleven local guild raids survive from 30 October through 18 December 2019. Outside reports begin eleven days later and follow a regular Sunday and Wednesday group through the opening months of Blackwing Lair.

By 29 April 2020 the trail becomes a named destination. Fifty-two of Nutellâ's later reports, across twenty-seven dates through 18 November, match Warcraft Logs' historical guild feed for Doubt. Her complete later history contains one hundred reports across sixty-three dates, but the Doubt matches are the part that establishes a guild rather than only continued activity.

nutfixer.name: Nutfixer
nutfixer.html: Nutfixer was an Ascension paladin with thirty-two guild raids between January and May 2020. Seventeen outside reports show an active history before his local debut, while eight more overlap the tenure. A single report one week after his final Ascension raid is the only later appearance.

néferti.name: Néferti
néferti.html:
Néferti was a druid who completed twelve Sleep raids and sixteen Dusk raids, plus one personal PUG, from July through November 2020. She was present for Dusk's first full Ahn'Qiraj clear. Six documented awards include early Cenarion pieces and Shimmering Geta.

Two outside reports overlap the tenure and two fall near its end. No wider destination trail survives.

obie.name: Obie
obie.html:
Obie was a mage in Ascension with ten guild raids from January through February 2020. Ten outside reports predate the local tenure and two overlap it.

Forty-five later reports return from August through December 2020. They establish a substantial later raid history, but the currently resolved metadata does not name its guild.

octocat.name: Octocat
octocat.html: Octocat raided as a hunter for Ascension across 56 raids between 23 October 2019 and 19 August 2020. Eighteen outside reports overlap the run, from 13 November 2019 to 19 August 2020, with none before or after. No landmark or loot award is documented.

ogetafix.name: Ogetafix
ogetafix.html: Ogetafix was a warrior in Ascension with thirteen guild raids from November 2019 through January 2020. No outside report appears anywhere in the completed character search.

oliveoyll.name: Oliveoyll
oliveoyll.html: Oliveoyll was a warrior with eleven Dusk raids and two personal PUGs during September 2020. Four awards include Doom's Edge, The Untamed Blade and Drake Talon Pauldrons. Three reports predate his local arrival, two overlap it, and one final appearance follows on 27 September.

opinummi.name: Opinummi
opinummi.html: Opinummi was a paladin in Ascension with twenty-seven guild raids from April through July 2020. Six external reports overlap that run. The completed search finds no activity before the local opening or after the final Ascension appearance.

orish.name: Orish
orish.html:
Orish, Dan on Discord, was the Thursday raid's healing brain and the most quotable internal critic the guild ever had. He came over with Ninjas, built the healer loot plans item by item, and leveled three warlocks just to run summons for other people's world buffs. He defended his turf in prose that still crackles: anyone trying to snake healing loot without knowing the role would "be dealing with me, one to one."

He fought with almost everyone worth fighting with: the priest channel, the Sunday-raid planners, and above all Divinestorm, in a September feud that produced the officer chat's most profane sentence. The thing about his criticism is that it was mostly right. The split-run chaos was real, the communication gaps were real, the members left in the dark were real. On 24 September 2020, undermined once too often on healer decisions, he quit live in the channel ("Leadership's going to run this guild into the ground, I'm out before it gets much worse") and took his alts with him. The officers restructured their entire chat within the hour. In a sense, that was his last accepted proposal.

outmageous.name: Outmageous
outmageous.html: Outmageous was a mage in Ascension's original recorded roster, with eighteen guild raids from October through December 2019. Two outside reports overlap that tenure. Seventy-two later reports then continue for almost ten months, revealing a major second raid history whose guild remains unresolved.

palaman.name: Palaman
palaman.html:
Palaman and the confirmed druid alt Drutt account for 96 alt-aware logged raids from 27 November 2019 through 25 November 2020. The class record spans paladin and druid, with 78 Sleep raids and 18 Dusk raids, and includes Sleep's first Nefarian kill. Across both characters, the loot trail contains 31 awards, notably Rejuvenating Gem on 25 March 2020, Lok'amir il Romathis in August, and healing gear from Ahn'Qiraj.

When Sleep reconsidered paladin leadership after Thepaladin lost access to the account, Palaman was one of the three documented candidates for the permanent class-leader seat. One outside report predates the local raid span and five external reports fall within it; those appearances show activity but not membership in another guild.

drutt.html:

palontras.name: Palontras
palontras.html:
Palontras was a paladin in Sleep with thirty-four guild raids from March through July 2020, plus one personal PUG. Fourteen documented awards trace his gearing through Molten Core and Blackwing Lair, beginning with Lawbringer Legplates and later including Pendant of the Fallen Dragon.

Unlike most of the roster, Palontras has no external Warcraft Logs trail in the completed character search. His surviving history lives entirely in the local archive.

panadin.name: Panadin
panadin.html:
Panadin was a paladin from the original friend group and the quieter half of Sleep's Eye of Sulfuras argument. By 27 March 2020 he had gathered all fifty Arcanite Bars for a Sulfuron Hammer. Artimis warned him that Thepaladin was fighting hard for the first Eye and asked what a guaranteed second drop would mean. Panadin accepted the second place because the other player was raiding more.

The queue flared again after Randyfist returned as paladin leader and announced a Ret switch. Artimis and Ragie held the earlier agreement. Panadin kept playing with the group outside raids too, organizing Among Us evenings through the autumn while Artimis was often busy farming AQ consumables or joining a pug.

pandaa.name: Pandaa
pandaa.html: Pandaa was a warrior in Ascension with thirteen guild raids from January through April 2020. Nine outside reports predate the local run and eight overlap it. No later appearance has been found.

pandemonio.name: Pandemonio
pandemonio.html:
Pandemonio was a rogue with ten Ascension guild raids and one personal PUG in the local archive. Two outside reports overlap the guild tenure.

The later history is much larger: seventy-four reports from September 2020 through March 2021. Most titles remain unresolved, so the evidence supports continued play but not a named destination.

panser.name: Panser
panser.html: Panser was a warrior with eleven Ascension guild raids and seven personal PUGs between May and November 2020. Two outside reports predate the guild tenure and ten overlap it. Twenty-three later reports continue from October 2020 through May 2021, documenting a substantial second raid history without a confirmed destination guild.

pasmaarop.name: Pasmaarop
pasmaarop.html:
Pasmaarop hunted for the guild across the Ninjas-to-Dusk transition and briefly for Ascension too: 24 raids with Dusk, 14 with Ninjas and four with Ascension, 42 total between 7 June 2020 and 13 January 2021. He was present for the 9/9 Ahn'Qiraj clear on 3 September and the first Dusk-only Naxxramas raid on 6 December, and drew five Ahn'Qiraj loot awards.

His attendance was thinner than his gear priority suggested. In November 2020, with only around 20 raids logged, he stood second in line for a full tier-3 set, a placement Artimis privately called "strange" to Zados and accepted only on condition Pasmaarop kept at least 70% attendance; Zados agreed to help him "improve his performance" in the meantime. By mid-December, with too many hunters competing for too few Naxxramas spots, Stormcat told him bluntly that he needed to show up "ready with consumes" and "pump hard to fight for a spot," and Artimis privately floated that Pasmaarop might be better off finding another guild while Dusk's roster stayed this tight. Fourteen outside reports overlap his run, ending 19 December 2020, with no reports afterward.

pawsz.name: Pawsz
pawsz.html:
Pawsz was a druid, a Ninjas officer, and the closest thing the officer chat had to a house intellectual — the one running the numbers on venom sac consumption per Viscidus attempt, proposing member polls with properly phrased questions, and arguing for radical transparency when everyone else wanted PR ("we can just let people read the officer chat. I don't care one bit how it looks"). His one-liners carried more policy than most meetings: "we are not the UN"; "Stoneshield is not something one pops for personal parsing."

He was also the merger's honest observer. It was Pawsz who noted the irony that the supposedly weaker Sleep brought the stricter rules, and Pawsz who refused to let September's departures become a Ninjas-versus- Sleep story: "We are not sat here pointing at Nayla either — why make this about Ninjas and Sleep again?" His final logged Dusk raid was on 24 September, and outside reports begin five days later. A targeted pass finds 108 later reports across sixty-six dates, most often alongside Banamahs and Antzi. The reports run through several uploaders and include explicit PUG titles, supporting a stable raid circuit rather than a named destination guild. None matches Decimation's thirty-eight-report historical guild feed. The archive does not preserve a departure message.

phrkica.name: Phrkica
phrkica.html:
Phrkica was a druid in Sleep with twenty-nine guild raids and one personal PUG from May through July 2020. Twenty-one documented awards begin with three Cenarion pieces on his first night and trace a concentrated gearing run through the summer.

Three outside reports overlap the tenure. Two more on 22 July are the only later activity found.

piromanzu.name: Piromanzu
piromanzu.html: Piromanzu was a rogue in Ascension's opening roster with twelve guild raids from October through December 2019. No outside report appears anywhere in the completed character search.

pnats.name: Pnats
pnats.html:
Pnats was a resto druid, Ragie's brother, and the officer chat's conscience. With 132 raids behind him he had the standing to say uncomfortable things, and he used it. When Artimis was benched in December, it was Pnats who opened the debate: the value the man had brought to Sleep and Dusk deserved better. When the officers needed someone to state the hard truth about Glory, he did that too, in words that were kinder in intent than on the page.

He was one of the few constants across the whole run, from Sleep through Dusk and into the first joint raid under Ascension. He healed Sleep's raids from 2 January 2020. The first surviving nomination for a healing-leader role came from Thepaladin on 15 March 2020: "maybe pnats would be good." Pnats became a Dusk officer at the September meeting, worried constantly about healer recruitment ("we lost so many healers"), and kept the loot log honest. He also supplied the archive's comic relief (the discovery that Missdotty was not, in fact, a woman cost him a genuine crisis of confidence) and its most quoted line: on the day Dusk dissolved, he pinged the officers with "BYE DUSK?" and then, at midnight, wrote the era's epitaph: "its been good Sleep > Dusk > Ascension, we've done it all =)"

He remained through the first joint Dusk-Ascension raid on 20 December 2020, logged onto his brother's warrior when the roster needed it, and stayed the person people forwarded screenshots to when something dramatic happened — which, in this guild, was often.

poison.name: Poison
poison.html: Poison was a rogue in Ninjas with twenty guild raids from March through May 2020. Nine outside reports predate that tenure and eight overlap it. After nearly a year of silence, one report on 16 May 2021 provides the only later trace.

potema.name: Potema
potema.html:
Potema's first appearance in the surviving guild records is a set of three Blackwing Lair awards on 13 May 2020. On 5 June, Rocka discussed bringing him into the roster as a new warlock. Potema went on to raid 46 times for Dusk and Sleep. Two personal PUGs and one joint Dusk-Ascension raid bring his total to 49, including the first Dusk-only Naxxramas raid on 6 December. He drew twenty-five loot awards across Molten Core, Blackwing Lair and Ahn'Qiraj, more than almost any other warlock in this batch.

He was good enough at the class to be a fixture of officer log reviews: in August 2020 Pawsz praised how fast he reacted with Searing Pain to keep threat off the healers during Chromaggus practice. By autumn he had become part of the small warlock core, alongside Rocka, Mounaros and Missdotty, that the officers rotated through a single lock spot every week, a rotation Divinestorm and Decretum discussed at length in December as Naxxramas attendance tightened. Nine outside reports precede the June recruitment discussion, two more overlap the run, and eleven pick up again in March and April 2021 without naming a guild.

powerranger.name: Powerranger
powerranger.html: Powerranger was a paladin in Ninjas with twenty-seven guild raids from February through July 2020. Fifteen outside reports precede the local tenure and twelve overlap it, showing an established raid history before Ninjas. No later appearance has been found.

pricelez.name: Pricelez
pricelez.html:
Pricelez was a rogue with 98 logged raids between 13 November 2019 and 2 September 2020, 94 with Sleep and four with Dusk. The first appearance is Sleep's earliest surviving 10/10 Molten Core report, followed days later by the first surviving logged Onyxia kill; Pricelez also attended the first Nefarian kill. Six recorded awards include four Bloodfang pieces, Band of Accuria, and Vek'lor's Diadem.

When the rogue class-leader position opened in July, Artimis asked Pricelez to take it, but Pricelez declined. The archive does not preserve a departure message and therefore does not establish why the final logged raid falls where it does. Two outside reports precede the Sleep span and one follows it, evidence of activity rather than a destination guild.

priestå.name: Priestå
priestå.html:
Priestå raided as a priest across Ninjas, Dusk, and joint Dusk-Ascension groups, for 55 raids between 6 August 2020 and 13 January 2021 (36 with Dusk, five each with Ascension and joint raids, five personal PUGs, four still under the Ninjas banner). He caught the first C'Thun and Ouro kills on 23 August, the 9/9 Ahn'Qiraj clear on 3 September, both Naxxramas firsts in December, and the Kel'Thuzad kill itself, drawing thirteen loot awards including four Naxxramas tier pieces in his final month.

He came out of Ninjas with a reputation attached: Decretum recalled in December 2020 that he'd once ragequit after a careless pull wiped a raid and cost him his Dark Master's Tarot buff. Supplier pushed to give him a formal Dusk raider spot that October, arguing the guild needed the extra priest more than another warlock. Priestå wanted to reroll shadow that November, but Supplier and Divinestorm decided a proven healer was worth more than an unproven third shadow priest, so he stayed holy and instead earned nominations for the Twisting Nether trinket and Sapphiron's Right Eye. His healing wasn't flawless: on the first Loatheb attempt that December, Supplier noted he started his heal eight seconds late because a lingering debuff had thrown off the timing. Eight outside reports predate his local run and eight more overlap it, ending 3 December 2020, with none afterward.

proctologist.name: Proctologist
proctologist.html:
Proctologist ran Sleep's mages with a methodical style. He tested whether absent players still read Discord and staged promotions during raids so they would feel meaningful. The class moved with little public drama.

The exception was Divinestorm. In April 2020 Divinestorm challenged the class leadership and took the case directly to Artimis. Proctologist thought he "just realy wants to be CL," but offered to step down if it meant one less problem for the guild. Artimis privately preferred to keep him. The officers chose Divinestorm, making Proctologist's restrained exit the first step in the next guild master's rise.

progres.name: Progres
progres.html: Progres was a warrior in Ascension with twenty-five guild raids from January through April 2020. Sixteen outside reports predate the local run and fourteen overlap it. The completed search finds no later appearance.

propalica.name: Propalica
propalica.html:
Propalica was a Ret paladin trying to fit into a roster whose four paladin spots were reserved for healers. He worked shifts around raids, but still watched newer players reach raider rank first despite arriving prepared. His protest was direct: if attendance could never overcome class composition, what message did the rank system send?

The argument with Artimis ranged from Onyxia heads to what loot was for. Artimis said it should go where it helped the guild most. Propalica answered that mechanics and preparation mattered too, especially for a Ret paladin who also healed and dispelled. They did not agree on every premise, but they settled the dispute.

In May work made regular raiding impossible. Propalica asked to be demoted rather than leave the guild planning around him. Artimis thanked him for being the first person to say so instead of simply disappearing.

psxycho.name: Psxycho
psxycho.html: Psxycho was a rogue in Ninjas. He completed thirty-four guild raids from February through July 2020 and appears once more in a personal PUG. Eighteen outside reports overlap that tenure. Four later reports, all in the following twelve days, show a short continuation but not a named destination.

psykos.name: Psykos
psykos.html: Psykos raided as a druid for Ascension 62 times between 6 October 2019 and 3 January 2021, including two personal PUGs and one joint Dusk-Ascension raid. Thirty-two outside reports overlap the run, from 13 November 2019 to 18 November 2020, with none before or after. No landmark or loot award is documented.

qiqi.name: Qiqi
qiqi.html:
Qiqi played a warlock main with a rogue alt, Zizy, confirmed by a loot-workbook comment naming Qiqi on one of Zizy's rows. As Qiqi he raided 48 times for Sleep between 20 November 2019 and 6 May 2020, present for the first Nefarian kill and the first full Zul'Gurub clear, and drew five loot awards including Mantle of the Blackwing Cabal and two Ebony Flame Gloves-tier drops.

He raided well enough, and geared up fast enough, that it became a talking point. Rocka's loot log shows him picking up Ebony Flame Gloves in March 2020 and pursuing a matching Tier 2 shoulder piece alongside Rocka the following month; by late April, Shakey was telling Artimis that officers were "pumping Qiqi with items" to the point that the guild's shadow priest "wont even get a look in." No outside reports exist before, during, or after his run.

ragie.name: Ragie
ragie.html:
Ragie, Pnats's brother, was the guild's tank spine across every era. Exclus referred him on 23 October 2019 as "a really good tank," before Ragie's first logged raid. He inherited the main-tank mantle when Kugel vanished in early 2020, and from then on the records rarely show a serious raid without him. An outside healer sent Sleep a tank-switch video during the first BWL week; Ragie turned the advice into positioning, then crafted the Dark Iron pieces that got the tanks through Firemaw. By the Dusk era he held the formal tank-leader role and ran Sunday raids alongside Snjór.

He is also half of the guild's longest loot argument. What does a main tank deserve first claim on: mitigation gear, crafting materials, a Thunderfury? The question put him repeatedly opposite Glory, whose complaint that "Ragie gets anything he wants" dates to March 2020. The archive is fairer to both men than they were to each other. Ragie's gearing was policy, argued openly in officer channels, and the binding runs that completed Thunderfuries were organised for him and others by name.

He was in the first Four Horsemen kill and the 15/15, made the move to Ascension on migration day (Pnats pinged him to take one last look at the dying Dusk channel), and kept tanking into 2022 in the guild's afterlife.

rakaiah.name: Rakaiah
rakaiah.html:
Rakaiah played priest through Ascension's final year, raiding 51 times between 12 July 2020 and 11 April 2021, two of them joint Dusk-Ascension runs, and stood in the roster for the Kel'Thuzad kill on 20 December.

She left Ascension before the eventual split was even announced, telling the post-Ascension officer chat in May 2021 that she'd gone "due to the amount of toxic people I don't want anything to do with." In the weeks after, while officers debated what to call the new guild forming out of Dusk and Ascension's remnants, she supplied the name Sanguine ("my favourite gecko"), joked about appointing herself guild master, and admitted she wasn't sure she wanted to stay a priest for the Burning Crusade expansion because she'd lost motivation. Six outside reports predate her local run, 23 overlap it, and nine more continue into May 2021, matching her visible presence in that same officer chat.

ramlösa.name: Ramlösa
ramlösa.html: Ramlösa raided as a mage for Ascension across 48 raids between 23 February and 26 July 2020, one of them a personal PUG. Eight outside reports overlap the run, from 26 February to 1 May 2020, with none before or after. No landmark or loot award is documented.

randyfist.name: Randyfist
randyfist.html:
Randyfist, Randy, Trenfentson on Discord, is one of the archive's quiet constants. He was brought into officer meetings in December 2019 and led the paladins before Thepaladin. Burned out, he stepped away on 2 March 2020 before the planned Nightfall could be crafted for him. He returned in April and accepted the class-leader job again on the 22nd, after Thepaladin lost his account.

The return was not quiet. Eight days into the job he announced a Ret switch and challenged Panadin's Eye of Sulfuras queue, while Artimis and Ragie backed the earlier agreement. A month later Ragie tried to recruit Exclusafk out of Randy's paladin roster and onto a warrior. Randy called it "Warrior Syndrome": the best class, he said, had the worst manners. The disagreement ended without a rupture.

By late Dusk he had become the officer chat's resident hawk. When the December merge talks began, his counsel was piracy: "poach the benched Ascension raiders, cancel the merge, Ascension implodes, we get half their shit. Just like a good ol' divorce." Nobody took the advice. Everybody quoted it.

He recruited paladins when nobody else would ("Recruit yourself, Randy," Divinestorm shot back), then rerolled hunter and fell in love with the class. On 14 December he tanked the first Four Horsemen kill and received Corrupted Ashbringer from its chest. Two days later he asked the question that ended Dusk: "When we leaving and merging?" He answered it himself within twenty minutes. "Fuck it, get it over and done with." His OCD, he explained, flared at unresolved things.

rangah.name: Rangah
rangah.html: Rangah was a hunter in the Ascension lineage, logging 107 raids from 15 January 2020 through 14 April 2021. The record contains 102 Ascension sessions and five joint Dusk–Ascension raids, including the first joint Naxxramas night and the first Kel'Thuzad kill. Rangah received a Desecrated Girdle on 16 December. After the clear, Zados reported that Rangah wanted the other hunters to take further Tier 3 pieces first because Rangah already had Rank 13 gear. Outside reports add 16 appearances before the span, 29 during it, and two afterward, but do not establish guild affiliation.

rat.name: Rat
rat.html: Rat was a rogue in Sleep with twelve guild raids during March 2020. The Head of Nefarian is his sole documented award. One outside report precedes the local debut by three days; none overlaps the tenure or follows it.

ravna.name: Ravna
ravna.html:
Ravna was a hunter on Sleep's original surviving roster. His twenty-eight guild raids begin with the first complete Molten Core report on 13 November 2019. Four days later he joined the first logged Onyxia kill, and in February he was present for the first Nefarian kill.

No outside report appears in the completed character search, so those local milestones define the entire surviving record.

redang.name: Redang
redang.html:
Redang healed as a priest for 54 raids between 13 February and 23 August 2020, 51 of them under the Ninjas banner and three after the Dusk merger, and was there for the first C'Thun and Ouro kills on 23 August.

Officers rated him one of their most dependable healers. In April 2020, Silveh named him alongside Dragonslay as the two candidates for priest class leader; a month later Dan singled him out after a clean Molten Core run, writing that "Redang is always on top of MC dispels" and that he was sad whenever Redang missed a raid. By September, a departing officer summed him up simply as "such a good healer who has been with us almost 100% of the time." Eleven outside reports predate his run, 18 overlap it, ending 28 June 2020, with none afterward.

reiner.name: Reiner
reiner.html: Reiner was a rogue with 132 logged raids between the first on 8 December 2019 and the last on 11 April 2021. Most belong to Sleep and Dusk, followed by 23 Ascension raids and five joint Dusk–Ascension sessions. Reiner attended the first Nefarian kill, Dusk's opening Naxxramas raid, the first joint raid, and the first Kel'Thuzad kill. Sixteen documented loot awards trace that progression from Bloodfang pieces and Band of Accuria to Chromatically Tempered Sword and a Desecrated Helmet.

rendhammer.name: Rendhammer
rendhammer.html: Rendhammer was a paladin in early Ascension. His thirty-one guild raids run from October 2019 through March 2020, with seven outside reports overlapping the same period. No report appears before the local record or after his final raid.

rockafella.name: Rockafella
rockafella.html:
Rockafella was a warlock and one of the guild's institutionalists. He asked Artimis for an Alterac Valley queue bot in December 2019, covered officer meetings for warlock leader Amandil, and later coordinated the class loot with Lyvana. When the mages debated replacing Proctologist, Rockafella gave Divinestorm the strongest peer endorsement: he had "always been wondering why he wasnt the Class Leader from the beginning."

In Dusk he was the voice that said the quiet part about governance out loud: "Class leaders think they are officers. If the class leaders could shut their mouths and run their class and let the officers manage the guild, we wouldn't have this shit." Within the hour, the officers split the chat in two. Few messages in the archive changed more structure faster.

He shows up wherever the record needs a witness with standing: talking Nayla's case through with Divinestorm and establishing that the infamous AQ20 "ninja pull" was a hearthstone misunderstanding; holding the line in the Band of Accuria fight ("we're trying to move away from a culture where the one who shouts loudest is right"); and tanking in the first Four Horsemen kill. He wanted a guild run by its officers, and mostly, after September, he got one.

During the December collapse he kept mailing alchemy materials to the benched Artimis. At 23:31 on migration night, while Dusk disappeared around them, Rockafella was still asking whether Artimis could make two flasks.

roddish.name: Roddish
roddish.html: Roddish raided as a rogue for Ascension across 43 raids between 15 January and 19 July 2020. Fifteen outside reports predate the run and 13 more overlap it, ending 8 April 2020, with none afterward. No landmark or loot award is documented.

rotato.name: Rotato
rotato.html: Rotato was a warlock in Ascension with fifteen guild raids from June through September 2020. One outside report overlaps that tenure. No activity has been found before the local opening or after the final raid.

ryba.name: Ryba
ryba.html: Ryba was a mage whose 71 logged raids, every one classified to Ascension, run from 15 January to 7 December 2020. The inventory records no landmark raid or loot award for the character. A broader report search found seventeen appearances before the logged span, between 6 November 2019 and 8 January 2020, and 21 external reports running from 23 February to 18 November 2020, evidence of activity rather than a named guild.

saltyhead.name: Saltyhead
saltyhead.html: Saltyhead was a rogue from the Ascension side of the archive, with 121 logged raids between 20 November 2019 and 11 April 2021. Of those, 114 are Ascension sessions, five are joint Dusk–Ascension raids, and two are personal pugs. Saltyhead attended the first joint Naxxramas raid and the first Kel'Thuzad kill, receiving Desecrated Pauldrons on 9 December and Kiss of the Spider four days later. The outside-report probe also found 51 external reports during the logged span and one afterward, evidence of activity rather than membership in any particular guild.

saltylock.name: Saltylock
saltylock.html:
Saltylock was a priest with twenty-two Ascension guild raids and seven personal PUGs between April 2020 and April 2021. Thirteen reports predate that local span and thirty-six overlap it, showing that most of his raid history lived outside the collected Ascension reports.

Six later appearances continue into May 2021. They document activity but do not identify another guild.

schokur.name: Schokur
schokur.html: Schokur was a priest in Ascension's opening roster with ten guild raids from November through December 2019. Two outside reports predate the local run and two overlap it. No later appearance has been found.

seax.name: Seax
seax.html:
Seax was a rogue from the Ninjas line. When he was still fighting for a regular Blackwing Lair place, Celed described him as motivated, prepared him for the bosses and offered his own seat so Seax could prove himself. He went on to complete fifty-six Ninjas and Dusk raids, including the first C'Thun kill and the first full Ahn'Qiraj clear.

Seax's final Dusk raid was 24 September 2020. His later trail contains fifty-four reports across thirty-three dates, with Celed present on twenty-seven. Forty-five reports across twenty-six dates match Warcraft Logs' historical guild feed for Agile, confirming the destination from 6 October through February 2021. Later appearances shift into PUG and GDKP runs.

selephie.name: Selephie
selephie.html:
Selephie raided as an Ascension paladin for 49 raids between 29 March 2020 and 11 April 2021, five of them joint Dusk-Ascension runs including the first on 9 December, and stood in the roster for the Kel'Thuzad kill eleven days later.

The archive shows an unusually active parallel life alongside the guild raids: 82 outside reports overlap the local tenure, far more than typical for this batch, on top of four personal PUG raids inside the guild's own logs, suggesting a player who filled spare nights with pickup groups alongside the scheduled Ascension roster. In December 2020, during a gear-level discussion, Trenfentson used Selephie's 75 item level as the reference point for how much a couple of item levels could matter. One outside report predates the run and 13 more continue from mid-April into May 2021, with no destination guild named.

servus.name: Servus
servus.html: Servus was a rogue in Sleep with thirteen guild raids during the summer of 2020. Bloodfang Gloves and Nightslayer Bracelets are his two documented awards. One report precedes the tenure, one overlaps it, and one isolated appearance follows in April 2021.

shadowheart.name: Shadowheart
shadowheart.html:
Shadowheart was a warlock in Sleep who made one further appearance after the Dusk merger. His thirty-three guild raids run from April through August 2020. Eleven documented awards chart a fast gearing path that began with Felheart Robes and Nemesis Leggings and included Azuresong Mageblade.

No outside report appears anywhere in the completed character search, so his entire surviving history comes from the local archive.

shakeyhealer.name: Shakeyhealer
shakeyhealer.html: Shakey was a priest, an officer, and one of the guild's steady hands — the kind of presence who appears in every era's records without ever being the problem. In the Glory affair he was one of the two named supporters ("Zados and Shakey has always been for you," Artimis told Glory on the night he quit), and his healing anchored the December raids: he is in the first Four Horsemen kill roster and stayed through the clear. His DM thread with Artimis is one of the largest in the archive — 562 messages of guild logistics across the whole of 2020 — and one of the least dramatic, which is its own kind of biography. When a stranger logged into Thepaladin's stolen account and quit the guild, Shakey and Luivi were the two who noticed and warned him.

shaolin.name: Shaolin
shaolin.html:
Shaolin healed as an Ascension paladin for 70 raids between 29 December 2019 and 3 January 2021, three of them joint Dusk-Ascension runs including the first one on 9 December 2020, and was in the raid for the Kel'Thuzad kill eleven days later. His single logged loot award, an Eye of Diminution, came from that same Naxxramas night.

He carried officer-level weight without an official title: Stormcat described him in mid-December as "just a healer and officer, not a specific healer officer," and Decretum had to ask around to confirm he was even Ascension's healing lead. His healing wasn't immune to review, either; on the first Loatheb attempt that December, Supplier logged that Shaolin started casting his heal eight seconds after Priestå, with Hedara shapeshifting to cover the gap. Twenty-nine outside reports overlap his entire run, from 9 January to 28 December 2020, with none afterward.

shaoxin.name: Shaoxin
shaoxin.html: Shaoxin was a druid who completed twenty-three Ninjas raids and eleven Dusk raids in the summer of 2020. He was present for the first C'Thun and Ouro kills and Dusk's first complete Ahn'Qiraj clear. Ten outside reports overlap the tenure, while one final report follows three days after his last Dusk raid.

shosanna.name: Shosanna
shosanna.html: Shosanna was a priest whose nineteen guild raids touched Sleep, Ninjas and Dusk. She joined Dusk's first complete Ahn'Qiraj clear and received Band of Dark Dominion followed by Cloak of Clarity. Three reports predate her local tenure, four overlap it, and one final appearance follows in September.

sitor.html: Sitor was a warrior in Ninjas with fifteen guild raids from March through April 2020. Eight outside reports overlap the tenure. Nine later appearances begin immediately afterward and stretch into May 2021, but the sparse trail does not identify a destination guild.

skogsluwder.html: Skogsluwder was a druid in Ascension with ten guild raids from May through June 2020. Two outside reports overlap the tenure. No activity has been found before the local opening or after the final raid.

smacky.name: Smacky
smacky.html: Smacky was a warrior in Ninjas with seventeen guild raids from late April through June 2020. Four external reports overlap that short tenure. The completed search finds no activity before the local opening or after the final raid.

smeggleswart.name: Smeggleswart
smeggleswart.html: Smeggleswart raided as a mage for Ascension across 50 raids between 15 January and 16 September 2020. Sixteen outside reports predate the run and 16 more overlap it, ending 9 September 2020, with none afterward. No landmark or loot award is documented.

smucky.name: Smucky
smucky.html: Smucky was a warrior from the Ninjas line who continued into Dusk, logging 73 raids from 13 February to 24 September 2020, split 57 to Ninjas and 15 to Dusk with one personal pug. Smucky was in the raid for the first C'Thun and Ouro kills and the first complete 9/9 Ahn'Qiraj clear, though no loot award is currently documented. A September 2020 Discord admin-role review named Smucky, alongside Artimis, Zados, Celed, and Antzi, among the longtime members whose server admin rights were flagged for removal. Smucky's final logged raid, 24 September 2020, falls on the date research into the era identifies as the point when nearly the entire former-Ninjas core stopped appearing in Dusk's logs. Eleven external reports predate the logged span, 25 more run alongside it, and one follows on 27 September 2020; they show activity, not a named destination guild.

snjór.name: Snjór
snjór.html:
Snjór, with Fantur as his warrior alt, came from Iceland with the Ninjas, held their raid leadership, and owned the Dusk Discord server itself. His tank career is the guild's clearest document of what off-tanking actually cost in Classic. Asked to hold Twin Emperors on a second-string gear set, he laid out the math (5,000 gold of Edgemaster's, double consumables, 5,900 health against 5,000-damage strikes) and then delivered the year's most quietly devastating line: "I've been saying this for weeks, and the answer was like, yeah, we can get someone else to do it."

He led Sunday raids, recruited half the server's strays, took responsibility for things that weren't his fault ("I told them to direct their anger at me"), and became the center of the era's worst day when Yeat kicked him on 30 September. Henne said someone then reinvited him and that he, or his alt, kicked her; his later account disputed the surrounding blame. The archive establishes the opening kick and the restriction of kick powers that followed, but not the full sequence or authorization. His summary of guild philosophy outlived all of it: "the mentality we set in Ninjas was always entertainment before some purple pixels."

On 1 October Luivi wrote that Missdotty had told him Snjór joined Agile. The next message separated the fate of his warrior: "No idea if Fantur stays or leaves." The logs complete that small split ending. Snjór's outside reports begin on 29 September, while Fantur continued raiding with Dusk through 21 October.

sofiero.name: Sofiero
sofiero.html: Sofiero raided as a hunter for Ascension across 57 raids between 27 November 2019 and 6 September 2020. One outside report predates the run and eight more overlap it, ending 23 August 2020, with none afterward. No landmark or loot award is documented.

sokrush.name: Sokrush
sokrush.html:
Sokrush was a mage who completed fourteen Sleep raids and five Dusk raids, plus one personal PUG, between May and December 2020. He stayed through Dusk's first guild-only Naxxramas night. Seventeen awards include Netherwind Crown and Fire Runed Grimoire.

Five reports predate his local arrival and eight overlap it. One joint Dusk-Ascension report on 9 December is the final outside appearance found.

sokrushl.name: Sokrushl
sokrushl.html:
Sokrushl was a warlock who completed ten Sleep raids and eighteen Dusk raids from July through November 2020. Fifteen documented awards include Shadow Wing Focus Staff and Band of Dark Dominion from his first Blackwing Lair weeks.

Three outside reports overlap the local tenure. No later activity has been found after his final Dusk appearance.

sonofglóin.html: Sonofglóin was a warrior in Ascension with twenty-one guild raids from March through May 2020. Eighteen outside reports predate his local arrival and three overlap the tenure. The wider search finds no later activity.

sourcer.name: Sourcer
sourcer.html: Sourcer was a paladin in Ascension with thirty-seven guild raids from March through October 2020. Six outside reports predate his local arrival and seven overlap it. spaxi.name: Spaxi
spaxi.html:
Spaxi was a rogue who joined the Ninjas raid in June 2020 and stayed into Dusk's final autumn. Celed argued for giving him a chance in Blackwing Lair, then included him in the group preparing nature-resistance gear for Ahn'Qiraj. Spaxi completed forty-four guild raids through 28 October and was present for Dusk's first full clear of Ahn'Qiraj.

His later history contains seventy-four reports across sixty-one dates. Forty-four dates overlap Ströheim, mostly in the Synai-uploaded Naxxramas roster. The final months branch into PUG and GDKP runs, including two Safe Haven BWL reports. Two reports across two dates also match Decimation's historical guild feed, showing that he sometimes raided with Decimation. The continuity identifies recurring raid communities, but no source confirms a destination guild.

specting.name: Specting
specting.html: Specting raided as a warlock for Ascension, logging 80 raids between 6 October 2019 and 3 March 2021, 78 of them Ascension sessions and two on the joint Dusk–Ascension roster. The record carries no landmark raid or loot award for the character. Fourteen external reports fall inside that span, from 17 November 2019 to 17 February 2021, evidence of continued Warcraft activity rather than membership in another guild.

stahlmarck.name: Stahlmarck
stahlmarck.html: Stahlmarck was a warrior in Ascension with thirty-one guild raids between January and June 2020. Seven outside reports predate his local arrival and eight overlap the tenure. The wider search contains no later appearance.

steewiee.name: Steewiee
steewiee.html: Steewiee and the confirmed alt Steewie were rogue and warrior characters with 84 alt-aware logged raids, from the first on 15 January 2020 to the last on 18 October 2020. Eighty of those raids are Ascension sessions, with four personal pugs, and no landmark or loot award is currently documented for either character. Across the two names, the Destiny classification totals sixteen before-tenure reports between 6 November 2019 and 8 January 2020, 35 external reports during the logged span running to 4 October 2020, and 143 after-tenure reports from 22 October 2020 to 18 May 2021; those numbers establish activity, not guild membership.

ströheim.name: Ströheim
ströheim.html:
Ströheim was a warrior from the Ninjas line. He logged forty-eight Ninjas and Dusk guild raids from February through 24 September 2020, including the first C'Thun and Ouro kills and the first full Ahn'Qiraj clear. By July the officers counted him among only six active damage warriors.

Outside reports resume three days after his final Dusk raid. The later history contains seventy-nine reports across sixty-eight dates, with forty-four later dates also appearing in Spaxi's post-tenure trail. Synai uploaded most of their Naxxramas run, while later reports move into explicit PUG and GDKP titles. Ströheim also appears throughout the named Safe Haven BWL series. One report also matches Decimation's historical guild feed, showing that he raided with Decimation at least once. Neither recurring community has a matching Razorgore guild record, so the archive does not assign him a destination guild.

stuntz.html: Stuntz was a warrior in Ascension's original recorded roster. His nineteen guild raids span October through December 2019. No outside report appears anywhere in the completed character search.

stylgar.name: Stylgar
stylgar.html: Stylgar raided as a paladin for Ascension, logging 71 raids from 15 January to 7 December 2020, all but one of them Ascension sessions and the remainder a personal pug. The record shows no landmark raid and no loot award for the character. Seventeen external reports run alongside the logged span, from 12 February to 30 November 2020, and 34 more follow from 14 December 2020 to 29 April 2021. They establish continued activity, not a named destination guild.

sudeki.name: Sudeki
sudeki.html:
Sudeki was a druid in Dusk's final roster. Eighteen Dusk raids, one joint night and one Ascension raid form his guild record, with three personal PUGs also preserved. He joined Dusk's first guild-only Naxxramas run, and eleven awards include Stormrage Boots and Shroud of Pure Thought.

Two reports predate his local arrival and five overlap it. Two isolated appearances on 13 May 2021 are the only later activity found.

supervillain.name: Supervillain
supervillain.html: Supervillain was a warlock in Ascension with sixteen guild raids from October through December 2019. One outside report overlaps the tenure. Thirty-three later reports resume in March and continue through June 2020, showing sustained activity without a named destination.

supplier.name: Supplier
supplier.html:
Supplier earned his name. Across three years and nearly a thousand messages with Artimis, he was the guild's consumables economy in human form: flasks, protection potions, world-buff logistics, the LBRS venom-sack supply chain that made Viscidus killable. If a raid had what it needed, odds are Supplier had something to do with it.

He was Norwegian, precise, and allergic to sloppy thinking. He asked what a poll was actually for before letting anyone run it. He told his fellow priests exactly how their channel would be run ("take it up with me directly"), and he de-escalated the guild's worst arguments by explaining what an expression had actually meant in context. He was named Healing Officer at the September 2020 meeting and stayed in that seat through the December merge.

Two footnotes belong to him. His dry one-liner "Shosanna was the only priest that got an item yesterday, fyi" became the last straw in Orish's dramatic exit; his whole reaction to the fallout was "Allright, nice to meet ya". And in May 2021 he posted the "Dusk list": a set of tribute video links, one per guildmate, the closest thing the guild ever made to its own memorial before this site.

syressa.html: Syressa was a warrior with fifteen Ascension guild raids and four personal PUGs from August through November 2020. Ten reports precede the guild window and seven overlap it. No activity has been found after the final local appearance.

szata.name: Szata
szata.html:
Szata was an experienced priest from the Ninjas line. The local archive contains twelve of his raids from February through 1 May 2020. Near the end of that run, Snjór proposed that Szata take temporary charge of the priests, with another officer reinforcing his calls. It was a brief recorded tenure, but he had already become the standard for experience in that class group.

Five weeks after his final Ninjas report, Szata appears in Agile's historical Warcraft Logs feed. Sixty-seven of his ninety-one later reports belong to Agile, covering forty dates from 6 June 2020 through 18 February 2021. The trail runs from Blackwing Lair and Ahn'Qiraj into a fixed Naxxramas schedule, often alongside Celed, Snjór and Seax.

tahansfamilj.name: Tahansfamilj
tahansfamilj.html: Tahansfamilj was a warrior in Ascension with eighteen guild raids and one personal PUG between May and September 2020. Four outside reports overlap that period. The completed search finds nothing before it or after it.

tanasus.name: Tanasus
tanasus.html: Tanasus was a warrior in the Ascension lineage, appearing in 118 logged raids from 6 October 2019 to 14 April 2021. All but one of those sessions are classified as Ascension, with the remaining appearance in a joint Dusk–Ascension raid. The wider Warcraft Logs search adds 21 external reports during that span and one afterward, but those reports document activity only and do not establish another guild affiliation.

tantum.name: Tantum
tantum.html: Tantum was a mage in the Ascension lineage, logging 95 raids from 15 January 2020 to 11 April 2021. Eighty-seven of those sessions are Ascension raids, with five more on the joint Dusk–Ascension roster and three personal pugs. Tantum was in the raid for the first joint Naxxramas night on 9 December 2020 and for the first Kel'Thuzad kill eleven days later, where Tantum received Desecrated Sandals. A wider report search adds eleven appearances before the logged span, 39 external reports running through it to 4 April 2021, and two more shortly after the last raid; those reports establish activity, not membership in another guild.

taptum.name: Taptum
taptum.html:
Taptum was a warlock in Ascension's Naxxramas roster. His thirty-six guild raids include three joint nights with Dusk, the first of those on 9 December, and the first Kel'Thuzad kill. The Naxxramas awards record Desecrated Sandals, Desecrated Robe and Cloak of the Necropolis.

Twenty-four reports predate his local arrival and twenty-one overlap the tenure. Another twenty-two continue after the final Ascension raid through 15 May 2021, showing sustained later activity without a confirmed destination guild.

thepaladin.name: Thepaladin
thepaladin.html:
Thepaladin, Durm on Discord, was Sleep's paladin class leader for six weeks in the spring of 2020, and his 232-message thread with Artimis is one of the archive's richest seams. He was rich (the guild leader once asked, half in awe, where all the money came from), an alchemist, and the owner of the guild's first Sulfuron Hammer, forged by Glory, which put him first in line for the Eye of Sulfuras. Then Panadin got a hammer too, the rule became "everyone with the hammer rolls," and Durm's protest ("That doesnt make me happy ... Retadin mainspec tho and was first and so on") is the purest specimen of the guild's endless argument between earned priority and equal chance.

He got the class-leader job on 5 March ("It's your job now :p") and spent it designing debuff priorities and Lok'amir queues. He also bought a Nightfall after the officers had rejected funding a second one, then confessed that it had been sitting in his bags for a week. Sleep tested it in Molten Core on 15 March. The uptime was poor, Thepaladin did about 200 damage per second, and Artimis concluded a regular damage dealer would do 300. The legendary experiment lost to the spreadsheet.

The four paladin raid spots were all healers, which left Ret players arguing for a path into the roster. Thepaladin fought hard for first place in the Eye queue and won it after Panadin accepted the second Eye. Then he lost everything to a hacker in mid-April. Someone logged into his account, the tickets went nowhere, and the thief even quit the guild on his character while Luivi and Shakey watched. Exclusafk covered the class temporarily. His raid log simply stops on 8 April 2020, mid-story. More Classic careers ended his way than any other: not in drama, in a support queue.

thermi.html: Thermi was an Ascension warrior whose thirty-one guild raids stretch from January into October 2020. Sixteen external reports predate the local run and twenty-one overlap it. Despite that substantial earlier activity, no report has been found after his last Ascension appearance.

thomas.html: Thomas raided as a mage for Ascension, appearing in 79 logged raids between 30 October 2019 and 19 August 2020, 78 of them Ascension sessions and one a personal pug. The character's record includes no landmark raid and no loot award. Twelve external reports run alongside the logged span, from 13 November 2019 to 19 August 2020, showing activity rather than proving membership in another guild.

tikiwikiboom.html: Tikiwikiboom was a hunter in Ascension's opening roster, completing seventeen guild raids from October through December 2019. Two outside reports overlap the tenure and four more follow into January 2020.

The outside Warcraft Logs probe found 16 external reports during the same period and one after the final logged raid, showing further activity without establishing guild membership.

torkir.html: Torkir was a druid in the Ninjas roster, completing thirty-nine guild raids between February and June 2020. Eleven outside reports precede his local tenure and eighteen overlap it. The record ends with the Ninjas period: there is no later Warcraft Logs appearance in the completed character search.

toxii.html: Toxii was a mage in Ascension with eleven guild raids from January through February 2020. Seventeen outside reports predate the local tenure and four overlap it. No later appearance has been found.

traviar.html: Traviar was a mage in Sleep with ten guild raids from April through May 2020. Six documented awards began with two Primal Hakkari tokens and the Heart of Hakkar in Zul'Gurub. Two outside reports predate the local tenure; none overlaps it or follows it.

tripaloski.name: Tripaloski
tripaloski.html: Tripaloski was a warrior on Sleep's original surviving roster. His twenty guild raids begin with the first complete Molten Core report in November 2019 and continue through February 2020. No outside report appears anywhere in the completed search.

tsakimo.name: Tsakimo
tsakimo.html:
Tsakimo's first raid was BWL on 26 February 2020. His connection failed, the raid replaced him, and Artimis apologized for not waiting longer. "Dont worry bro im chill person," Tsakimo answered. It was his first raid anywhere, and he liked that Sleep explained what to do. He was promoted to raider on 18 March.

The calm had limits. In July the new rogue leader Twx replaced Kodf's round-robin system with performance loot. Tsakimo could not match the world-buff demands around work and family, so he quit on the 23rd. Divinestorm quietly recruited him back before Dusk formed. On 19 August, the first Dusk AQ40 night, Tsakimo asked for spreadsheet access and resumed recording loot. By November his message had changed to "parse time 99."

He ran the Wednesday rogues through the Dusk era, working the queue with Antzi across the two teams. His class-leader philosophy was transactional in the best sense: "loot is the reward, you make the effort, you focus, you pay for consumables, then you get loot." He handled the Nayla telephone-game with more patience than it deserved ("I will not take part in the insanity") and got a taste of the job's real burden when a relayed conversation turned out to have two versions. "Now you can feel how it's working," Luivi told him, and he laughed.

He was blunt about standards (sign up by Friday or lose your spot, "no exceptions") and blunt about himself, always discounting his own parses before anyone else could. The rogues under him stayed drama-free, which was the only metric he cared about.

tutpalacu.name: Tutpalacu
tutpalacu.html:
Tutpalacu was a paladin whose twenty guild raids divide evenly between Dusk and Ascension. He joined Dusk's first guild-only Naxxramas night. Eight documented awards include Vek'lor's Diadem, Skin of the Great Sandworm and Wormscale Blocker from the same November Ahn'Qiraj run.

Nine outside reports overlap the tenure. No report follows the final Ascension appearance.

twx.name: Twx
twx.html:
Twx joined Sleep in July 2020 with three raids behind him and a clear idea of how rogues should work. Seniority would not matter. Parses, world buffs, the right spec, and consumables would decide loot. Artimis warned that Sleep was not a hardcore guild, then gave class leaders room to run their own class. Twx accepted the job on 13 July.

The experiment lasted about three weeks. Twx awarded himself two tier pieces, put sword rogues first, and told the class that better performers would receive priority. Tsakimo left over the system. Ntekapaz brought the complaints to Artimis, who checked the performance claim against the logs and wished aloud for someone who could restore Kodf's queues.

Twx also pursued a Thunderfury, at one point planning to buy a Binding from a pug for 5,000 gold. He later claimed to own one already, but the officers never verified it. By the time Dusk formed he was gone, leaving behind the shortest and sharpest class-leader era in Sleep's record.

táyto.name: Táyto
táyto.html: Táyto was a warrior in Sleep with fourteen guild raids from March through May 2020. Six awards include Obsidian Edged Blade, Breastplate of Might and the Head of Onyxia. One outside report overlaps the tenure; none appears before it or after it.

ulfhild.name: Ulfhild
ulfhild.html:
Ulfhild was the guild's best hunter and made no apology for what that took: world buffs, full consumables, and total focus, every raid, for a character whose job was the damage meter. The Thursday team built its expectations around him, and he delivered so consistently that his one famous lapse became a governance crisis: on 17 September 2020, when a botched pull at the Ahn'Qiraj entrance wasted the buffs he'd spent hours collecting, he quit the raid on the spot.

The three-day officer argument that followed used his name as shorthand for a whole worldview. His defenders — and they were loud — pointed out that a near-perfect raider had been failed by the raid, not the other way around; his critics said no one player's buffs outweigh thirty-nine people's evening. He apologized in private, was back the next week, and kept doing what he always did: pulling, as one officer put it, more than his share. If everyone had pumped like Ulfhild, the mage leader mused that autumn, AQ would take forty-five minutes.

His final logged Dusk raid was 24 September. The later trail contains seventy-one reports across thirty-seven dates, forty-two uploaded by Ulfhild himself. Henne, Katdrovrsn, and Mikadrovrsn appear occasionally, but the recurring roster is mostly a separate outside circle. Fifteen reports across nine dates match Decimation's historical guild feed, showing that he repeatedly raided with Decimation. The wider record still supports an independent raid community rather than a wholesale re-formation of Ninjas.

verdish.name: Verdish
verdish.html: Verdish was a warrior in Ascension's opening roster with thirteen guild raids from November through December 2019. Two outside reports overlap the tenure and seven more continue into February 2020.

végeta.name: Végeta
végeta.html: Végeta was a rogue in Ninjas with twelve guild raids from February through April 2020. Eleven outside reports predate that tenure and eleven overlap it. No later appearance has been found.

wackd.name: Wackd
wackd.html: Wackd was a mage in Sleep with sixteen guild raids from December 2019 through February 2020. One outside report predates his local debut. Three later appearances are spread from the following week to March 2021, too sparse to define another raid community.

wapposo.name: Wapposo
wapposo.html: Wapposo was a mage in Ascension with twenty-four guild raids from February through May 2020. Five reports predate his local arrival and seven overlap the tenure. No activity has been found after the final Ascension raid.

wauki.name: Wauki
wauki.html: Wauki was a warlock with fourteen Ascension guild raids and four personal PUGs spread from March 2020 through March 2021. Two reports predate the local record and twenty-five overlap it. No appearance follows the final raid.

weeksea.name: Weeksea
weeksea.html: Weeksea was a warlock with fifteen Sleep raids, one Dusk appearance and one personal PUG. Fifteen documented awards begin with Felheart Horns, Felheart Slippers and Nemesis Leggings on the same March night. Four outside reports overlap the tenure; none follows it.

wehnergok.name: Wehnergok
wehnergok.html: Wehnergok raided as a rogue for Ascension across 47 raids between 15 January and 26 August 2020. Sixteen outside reports predate the run and 11 more overlap it, ending 23 August 2020, with none afterward. No landmark or loot award is documented.

wetfarter.name: Wetfarter
wetfarter.html: Wetfarter was a hunter with eleven Ascension guild raids and one personal PUG from June through September 2020. Two outside reports predate the guild tenure and six overlap it. No later appearance has been found.

xroth.name: Xroth
xroth.html: Xroth raided as a warlock for Ascension 54 times between 9 February and 23 August 2020, two of those personal PUGs. Four outside reports predate the run and 14 more overlap it, ending the same day as his final logged raid, with none afterward. No landmark or loot award is documented.

yealof.name: Yealof
yealof.html:
Yealof was a paladin who completed six Ninjas raids and sixteen Dusk raids, plus two personal PUGs, during the Ahn'Qiraj summer. He joined the first C'Thun and Ouro kills. Five documented awards include Neretzek, The Blood Drinker and Boots of the Redeemed Prophecy.

Ten reports predate the local tenure and five overlap it. No later appearance has been found.

yeat.name: Yeat
yeat.html:
Yeat was the Thursday team's raid leader and master looter — the warrior who actually ran the nights, kept the loot in his bags between raids (occasionally to the guild banker's despair), and dialed in from work trips with lines like "please make preparations as if I'm not there." His raid-leading philosophy hardened after the September pull crisis: stricter comms, less fun on the mic, "I don't want that in my raid, full stop."

His name is attached to the era's strangest day. On 30 September 2020 he kicked Snjór from the guild; that opening act is the one point both participant accounts share. The reinvite, Henne's subsequent kick, and the protest quits that followed nearly cracked the guild, but the surviving accounts do not establish the full sequence or blame. The reform that came out of it restricted kick powers for good. Yet the same record shows why he held the job: steady on loot fairness, first to volunteer for unglamorous logistics, and holder of the in-game guild-master character during the transition — which is how a mid-conflict kick became constitutionally possible in the first place.

yogini.name: Yogini
yogini.html: Yogini was a mage in Ascension with thirty-six guild raids from December 2019 through April 2020. Five reports predate the local record and three overlap it. One final outside appearance follows on 1 May; no broader later history has been found.

yumï.name: Yumï
yumï.html: Yumï was a hunter in Ninjas with eleven guild raids from May through July 2020. Three outside reports overlap that tenure. One isolated appearance on 26 February 2021 is the only later trace.

yungflexin.name: Yungflexin
yungflexin.html: Yungflexin was a paladin whose 80 logged raids, every one of them classified to Ascension, run from 23 October 2019 to 7 December 2020. Neither a landmark raid nor a loot award is currently on record for the character. A broader report search found 21 external appearances between 13 November 2019 and 9 September 2020, establishing activity during that window rather than membership in a named guild.

yúna.name: Yúna
yúna.html: Yúna raided as a rogue for Ascension thirty-seven times between February and June 2020. Eighteen reports predate that tenure and twelve overlap it, placing Ascension inside a longer existing raid history. Three appearances continue into August, but no named destination is preserved.

zados.name: Zados
zados.html:
Zados was the guild's other half of the hunter brain trust and its co-leader in everything but title. From late 2019 onward he shows up wherever decisions were made: running the hunter class and its loot queues, keeping the debuff-slot priority list current, arguing rules in the officer chat with a debater's stamina, and organising the three-week hunter rotation that he, Artimis and Nereb shared when spots got scarce. His pet did enough damage to become a running joke in feral-druid comparisons.

The Dusk era slowly squeezed the old Sleep leadership out of power, and Zados felt it first. In the September 2020 server reshuffle his admin rights were flagged for removal, and when Divinestorm deleted a channel he liked, his reply (that he supposed he wasn't an officer any more, so whatever) is the driest line in the whole archive. He kept working anyway: the debuff documentation, hunter loot calls, and the long Discord-ping culture war he fought on pure principle ("I'm completely basing my reasoning on logic").

In December he was in the room for everything: skeptical of the new partners ("I have a pretty bad impression of ascension players so far"), blunt about roster choices, and finally the one who answered "when are we leaving and merging?" with "today would be good." He was in the first Four Horsemen kill and the Kel'Thuzad clear — one of the few who was there from the first Molten Core to the last boss of Classic.

zarin.name: Zarin
zarin.html: Zarin raided as a rogue for Ascension across 52 raids between 27 November 2019 and 17 June 2020. One outside report predates the run, nine overlap it, and seven more continue from September through November 2020 without naming a destination guild. No landmark or loot award is documented.

zhèna.name: Zhèna
zhèna.html:
Zhèna was a warrior from the Nittedal circle who kept ending up in front of the boss when nobody else could. He became a full member on 16 February 2020 and stepped up as temporary main tank in the gap Kugel left. By July the Thunderfury plan had him next for a right-hand Binding after Glory and Ragie. He was still the tank the Thursday team missed months later, when a busy Wednesday forced an undergeared Snjór in front of the Twin Emperors. Fnats named him among the players who most deserved the Drake Fang Talisman: "top of the meters constantly, with attendance, consumables, world buffs."

He was also one of the guild's top damage dealers whenever he wasn't tanking, a two-hander enthusiast, and part of the Nittedal thread that runs through the whole story: his DM transcript with Artimis covers BWL preparation, binding-queue politics, and the ordinary friendship underneath ("I bought Diablo 4. I should never have done that," a later message confesses, from another game and another decade of the same crew).
